REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
recommendations/observations as contained in its Two Hundred Forty Fourth Report on Demands for
Grants (2017-18) of the Ministry of Civil Aviation which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament
on 17th March, 2017.
2. Action Taken Replies were received from the Government on 21st July, 2017, in respect of
all the recommendations/observations contained in the Report. The replies have been categorized as
follows:-
(i) Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
Paragraph Nos.: 10, 17, 19, 25, 27, 30, 33, 33B, 33D, 35, 37, 45, 46, 50, 53, 54, 56, 58,
Total: 26
(ii) Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of
the Government replies:-
Total: 3
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not
been accepted by the Committee:
Total: 5
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still
awaited.
Total: 13
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of those recommendations/observations
which have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished at the
earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of
Action Taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the Committee contained
in the Two Hundred Forty Fourth Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry and recommendations/
observations of the Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the succeeding
paragraphs:
ASSESSMENT OF THE DEMANDS FOR GRANTS (2017-18) OF THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee notes that ` 2702.40 crores has been allocated for the Ministry of Civil Aviation
for 2017-18 against the allocation of ` 3452.37 crores at RE stage in 2016-17. (Para 10)
61,  65,  78,  81,  82,  83,  85  and  86
Paragraph  Nos.:  22,  23  and  33F
Paragraph  Nos.  :  25A,  41,  72,  72A  and  73
Paragraph  Nos.:  14,  22A,  30A,  33C  ,  43,  48,  52,  63,  66,  76,  80,  81B  and  84

2
Reply of the Government
6. Noted.
Further Recommendations/Observations
7. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
8. The Committee notes that there is considerable shortfall in budgetary allocation for 2017-18
especially on the Revenue side and that the Ministry of Finance has not intimated any reason for this
reduction. Keeping in view the considerable growth of the civil aviation sector, Committee is of the
considered view that with the present allocation, it would be difficult to run the existing schemes and
other activities undertaken by the Ministry. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the Ministry
should actively pursue the matter of increasing the allocation in the first supplementary and at the RE
stage in the current financial year 2017-18, with the Ministry of Finance. (Para 14)
Reply of the Government
9. The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. The proposal for
increase in allocation of funds for Ministry of Civil Aviation for 2017-18 will be taken up with Ministry
of Finance through 1st Supplementary grant and at RE stage as well.
Further Recommendations/Observations
10. The Committee may be apprised of the progress made in this regard.
Recommendation/Observation
11. The Committee may be apprised of the details of the Skill Development Scheme at the implementing
stage. (Para 17)
Reply of the Government
12. The details of the Skill Development Scheme are given as under:-
(a) Ministry had engaged M/s iMaCS for conducting a comprehensive skill gap analysis and
future Road Map for skill development in Civil Aviation Sector. M/s iMaCS submitted the
final report on 15.03.2016.
(b) A workshop on raising awareness about National Skill Qualification Framework was held
on 20.10.2016 with training institutions.
(c) An MoU b/w MoCA and MSDE was signed on 20.10.2016 for collaboration on skill
development.
(d) A Workshop on Recognition of Prior Learning for Aviation Professionals in the Airline/
Airport/Ground Handling/MRO services was held on 08.02.2017. Further, through the
Workshop, Data Entry operators of Ministry of Civil Aviation, DGCA and BCAS have been
given training under RPL on 28th - 31st March, 2017.

3
(e) The skill development programme has been launched in the cargo sector with the introduction
of the Basic Cargo Awareness Programme (BCAP) programme at Joint Venture and AAI
Airports. The pilot BCAP was launched at Delhi i.e. IGIA Cargo Terminal on 20/10/2015.
(f) Industry validation of 38 QPNOS for civil aviation sector is in process by the AASSC and
they will be finalized in due course of time, after which NSQF aligned training can commence.
The first Executive Development Programme (EDP) was held by Rajiv Gandhi National
Aviation University (RGNAU) on 2-4 February 2017.
Further Recommendations/Observations
13. The Committee notes the reply.
TWELFTH FIVE YEAR PLAN
Recommendation/Observation
14. The Committee takes note of the projects initiated by the Ministry during the Twelfth Five year
Plan. (Para 19)
Reply of the Government
15. Noted.
Further Recommendations/Observations
16. The Committee notes the reply.
AIR INDIA LIMITED
Recommendation/Observation
17. The Committee feels that the reduction in equity infusion to the tune of Rs. 787 crores will
adversely affect the financial and operational performance of the company since it may be forced to take
loans from banks and financial institutions at a higher interest rate to meet the short fall, which was
not contemplated under the Financial Restructuring Plan. The Committee, therefore, is of the considered
view that such short fall, at this stage when the company is presently placed at a critical position in
achieving the TAP targets, should be avoided. Since the committed financial support from the Government
is vital to sustain the momentum of performance of Air India, the Committee strongly recommends that
the full amount of equity infusion should be restored to Air India. The Committee recommends that in
future, the amount committed under the TAP should be allocated to Air India at the BE stage itself.
(Para 22)
Reply of the Government
18. With regard to increase in allocation of funds for the current financial year, the matter has been
taken up with Secretary (Finance). However, a formal proposal for additional funds will be taken up at
the time of 1st Supplementary grant.
Further Recommendations/Observations
19. The Committee hopes that the amount committed under the TAP would be allocated to Air
India at the RE stage.

4
Recommendation/Observation
20. The Committee was informed by the Secretary that the profit of Air India has been severely dented
to the tune of ` 1000 crore due to rupee depreciation and foreign exchange variation. The Ministry of
Finance has not taken into account the factor of rupee depreciation and foreign exchange variation while
deciding the equity infusion. The Committee, therefore, recommends that if the intention of the Ministry
of Finance is the revival of Air India, then the former should seriously consider the factors which are
beyond the control of Air India such as depreciation of rupee and foreign exchange variation, while
deciding the amount of equity infusion. (Para 22A)
Reply of the Government
21. The Ministry of Civil Aviation has requested Air India to submit a proposal on the reduction in
profit due to rupee depreciation and foreign exchange variation. Once the proposal from Air India is
received, the matter will be taken up with Ministry of Finance.
Further Recommendations/Observations
22. The Committee may be apprised of the progress made in this regard.
Recommendation/Observation
23. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Civil Aviation may take up this matter
with the Ministry of Finance for the restoration of the full amount of Equity Infusion of 
` 2587 crores
as requested for in the Annual Plan for the financial year 2017-18 by Air India Ltd.
(Para 23)
Reply of the Government
24. The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. The proposal for
restoration of full amount of Equity infusion of ` 2587.00 crore for 2017-18 will be taken up with
Ministry of Finance through 1st Supplementary grant and at RE stage as well.
Further Recommendations/Observations
25. The Committee hopes that the amount committed under the TAP would be allocated to Air
India at the RE stage.
Recommendation/Observation
26. The Committee appreciates Air India for making operational profits in the financial year 2015-
16. The Committee hopes that Air India would register further profits in the coming months. The
Committee emphasizes the need for micromanaging routes and timings of Air India flights to make Air
India more competitive and passenger friendly. (Para 25)
Reply of the Government
27. Air India schedule is prepared on the basis of its independent assessment of demand, availability
of requisite resources and subject to allotment of the requisite time slots at the various airports. The

5
schedule preparation is aimed at optimizing the deployment of the airline’s resources in order to meet
demands and maximize profits. With the creation of Delhi as its main hub utmost importance is given
to provide seamless and convenient connections both for the domestic as well as international passengers
travelling on its flights. The schedule is drawn with the sole purpose of maximising the yield and
enhancing the revenue on the network by providing convenient connectivity. The feeder traffic to Air
India’s International and Domestic flights have grown over the period which has resulted in better
revenue generation.
28. Air India reviews the performance of its flights on a regular basis. The carriage / load factors /
financial performance of services on its network are regularly monitored and also efforts made to
improve their performance like increase or decrease frequency on existing routes /modifying the existing
schedule by changing the departure time or equipment on a particular route etc. Inputs and suggestions
from Sales and Marketing team regarding change in departure time of a particular flight are also analyzed
for enhanced revenue and implemented subject to availability of Slots at the Airports.
29. Major route restructuring was done in winter 15 schedule with an aim to operate point to point
flights to / from major hubs thereby increasing availability of aircraft and crew for optimum utilization
of available resources and increasing revenue.
30. Following main points are considered in managing the routes operated by Air India:
1. Serve Metro markets, which account for bulk of domestic traffic with multiple daily
frequencies.
2. Aim to serve all markets nonstop to the extent feasible / viable and restructure round robin/
one halt services to nonstop.
3. Aim to serve all markets with at least a daily service, subject to feasibility and viability.
4. Endeavour to provide day return connectivity which are already served with a daily service.
5. Focus on improving connectivity between DEL and other domestic points to strengthen the
hub at DEL.
6. Gain reasonable presence in the growing low cost market segments.
7. Develop new feeder networks to increase flows on trunk and metro routes with focus on
tier-II / tier-III cities.
Further Recommendations/Observations
31. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
32. During the deliberations of the Committee, many Members of the Committee have complained that
the catering services in Air India aircrafts are not up to the mark and that it needs improvement to attract
more passengers. The Committee notes that this is an oft repeated complaint which needs serious attention
of the top management of Air India and Ministry of Civil Aviation. The Committee urges upon the

6
Ministry to evaluate the standards of the catering services in Air India flights and take necessary steps
to improve the same. The Committee may be informed about the action taken in this regard.
(Para 25A)
Reply of the Government
33. Air India uplifts its meal from the reputed caterers on its flights who also cater to several domestic
and international airlines and have various requisite regulatory certifications and licences. The caterers
also undergo regular audits and checks from these regulatory bodies and Air India to ensure quality.
34. Meal service is reviewed from time to time and menus are updated as per sector-wise requirements
putting emphasis on regional cuisine and also taking into consideration duration of flight, flight timings
and local infra-structural & raw material availability. It is ensured that hygienic, palatable and wholesome
meals are provided to the passengers.
35. The views of the Committee members about quality of food are noted and the caterers would be
urged to ensure and improve quality.
Further Recommendations/Observations
36. The Committee notes that there is ample scope for improvement in the standards of
catering services made available in Air India flights.
AIRPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA
Recommendation/Observation
37. The Committee notes that earlier , the cargo sector was dominated by private airlines. The Committee
welcomes the entry of AAI into the cargo sector. (Para 27)
Reply of the Government
38. Noted.
Further Recommendations/Observations
39. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
40. The Committee feels concerned about the huge amount of outstanding dues of AAI for a long time.
AAI, being the highest revenue generator, has to be actively helped by the Ministry of Civil Aviation
in this regard by taking it up with the defaulting Organizations and Ministries including legal recourse.
The Committee recommends that consistent steps should be taken by AAI to recover the outstanding dues.
(Para 30)
Reply of the Government
41. Statement of dues of various major airlines and concessioners is enclosed at Annexure-A. It may
be seen that there is considerable improvement in recovery of dues in all cases. In case of National

7
Carrier (Air India Group) tripartite meeting was held on 1st March, 2017 with Air India officials along
with Ministry of Civil Aviation officials to expedite the settlement/clearance of dues. Action is being taken
up accordingly.
42. Other scheduled domestic operators are also being pursued to speed up the payment process. Dues
are being monitored closely. As suggested all the Regions/Airports have been instructed to closely monitor
the dues and to report immediately to CHQ in case of any major variation/delay in realization.
Further Recommendations/Observations
43. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
44. The Committee notes that ` 294.69 crores is due from now defunct Kingfisher Airlines. The
Committee also notes that legal suit has been filed against Kingfisher Airlines to recover the dues. The
Committee observes that the Airports Authority of India allowed the accumulation of dues to such a high
level in violation of all the existing rules and procedures in practice. The Committee recommends that
Airports Authority of India should be cautious in future to ensure that no individual stakeholder/airlines
is accumulating such high levels of dues. The Committee also recommends that Airports Authority of
India may conduct an internal inquiry (i) to fix the responsibility of Airports Authority of India officials
for the accumulation of dues by Kingfisher Airlines and (ii) to strengthen the systems and procedures to
prevent the recurrence of accumulation of dues. The Committee may be intimated about the outcome of
the internal inquiry. 
Reply of the Government
45. All Regional Hqrs. and airports have been instructed to ensure that such cases are not repeated
in future. An Internal Committee has been constituted in AAI headed by the senior officer to fix the
responsibility of the officials for the accumulation of dues by Kingfisher Airlines and to strengthen the
systems and procedures further to ensure prevention of recurrence of such accumulation of dues. On
receipt of the report of the said Internal Committee further action will be taken.
46. The dues of Private Concessioners have accumulated mainly because of Arbitration, Court cases,
service tax and royalty. All the cases are consistently being followed up. Government and other PSUs
are pursued with the respective Departments.
Further Recommendations/Observations
47. The Committee desires that strict action should be taken against the responsible officials
found guilty by the Internal Committee.
Recommendation/Observation
48. The Committee hopes that the monetization of AAI land will generate considerable revenue to AAI.
(Para 33)
Reply of the Government
49. Noted.
(Para  30A)

8
Further Recommendations/Observations
50. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
51. The Committee recommends that Airports Authority of India should take initiatives to establish
sufficient commercial activities at the Kolkata airport to generate reasonable level of non-aeronautical
revenue. The Committee is afraid that the neglect of the airport may be a prelude to making it a loss
making airport which may pave the way for privatization of services at the airport.
(Para 33B)
Reply of the Government
52. To optimize utilization of available space and to increase Non-aeronautical revenue, new licenses
for various facilities have been awarded since 2016. Details of major contract is appended below:
Sl. No. Facility Space Revenue
1. Duty Free Outlet 605 sqm. `1,84,43,840/- p.m
2. Master Concessionaire for General Retail 1050 sqm. ` 86,07,500/- p.m
3. Advertisement Rights 14697 sqm. `3,13,48,701/- p.m
53. For non-aeronautical revenue of Kolkata Airport is continuously increasing year by year with
following details:
2013-14 `178.46 Crores
2014-15 `217.63 Crores
2015-16 `257.99 Crores
54. Further, endeavor is being made to exploit the available space, without encroaching into passenger
convenience and safeguarding the safety concern by introducing various new licenses to enhance AAI
Non-aeronautical revenue and to improve passenger experience.
Further Recommendations/Observations
55. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
56. It has been brought to the notice of the Committee that Gir Forest which is one of the sanctuaries
for Asiatic Lion is a much visited area by the domestic as well as foreign tourists. However, there is no
air operations anywhere near the sanctuary. The Committee noticed that there is an airstrip near Gir
which can be developed to improve air connectivity. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Airports
Authority of India should take the lead to enable the Gir airstrip to start commercial air operations.
(Para 33C)

9
Reply of the Government
57. Airports Authority of India owns and maintains Keshod Airport near the Gir Forest which is
approximately 92 km by road and aerial distance of 40 NM (approx.). Keshod Airport is having a runway

EXORBITANT AIRFARES
Recommendation/Observation
122. The Committee takes note of the fact that there are no existing rules and regulations which are
working in the way of regulating airfares after the repeal of Air Corporation Act in 1994. The Committee
desires that the Ministry of Civil Aviation should specify the limitations, legal and otherwise, which need
to be amended or other measures to be put in place to tackle this problem after consulting all the
stakeholders. We are a developing country and many of the pricing mechanism applicable to the developed
countries may not suit the Indian people and Indian conditions. The Ministry should consider fixing an
upper limit for every sector, especially in the economy class of air fares. (Para 72)
Reply of the Government
123. Under the provision of Sub Rule (1) of Rule 135, Aircraft Rules 1937, airlines are free to fix
reasonable tariff having regard to all relevant factors, including the cost of operation, characteristics of
services, reasonable profit and the generally prevailing tariff. Air fare so established by the airlines is
published on their respective website under the provision of Sub Rule (2) of Rule 135, Aircraft Rules
1937.
124. In order to prevent excessive charging and sudden surges in airfares and to promote transparency
by scheduled domestic airlines, DGCA has also issued Air Transport Circular 02 of 2010 wherein airlines
are required to display on their respective websites the tariff sheet route-wise across their network in
various fare categories and the manner it is offered in the market. The intention behind the above
directions is to keep the passengers informed of pricing pattern of airlines. DGCA has also set up a Tariff
Monitoring Unit in 2010 that monitors airfares on certain routes selected on random basis to ensure that
the airlines do not charge airfares outside the range declared by them.

20
Further Recommendations/Observations

Reply of the Government
127. The routes between India and Gulf are characterized by a mix of Full service and Budget carriers.
On international routes, including Kerala - Gulf , the fares being offered are reasonable and have been
constructed based on market considerations such as fares offered by competitors, seasonality, extent of
competition and product features like frequency, timing’s, direct / indirect operations etc. All fares
offered by Air India are published fares with given validity and are not changed arbitrarily to take
advantage of holiday / festival season. Closer to departure higher fares may be available as low fares get
sold out first.
Further Recommendations/Observations
128. The Committee is not satisfied with the reply furnished by the Ministry. The Committee
may be apprised of the steps taken by the Ministry to ensure that the public is protected from
predatory airfares.
Recommendation/Observation
129. The Committee also notes that even after 50% reduction of the ATF prices over a period of time,
the airlines have not passed on the benefit of reduction in ATF prices to the consumers. The Committee
recommends that the Ministry should take effective steps to ensure that the airlines pass on the benefit
to the travellers by reducing the air fares and inform the Committee about the specific steps taken in
this regard and the outcome thereof. (Para 73)
Reply of the Government
130. Airfares are not regulated by the Government and airlines are free to fix reasonable charges/fee
subject to compliance with rule 135 of Aircraft Rules 1937. The prices are fixed by airlines keeping in
mind the market demand, seasonality and other market forces. Air fares established by the airlines under
the provision of Sub Rule (1) of Rule 135 of Aircraft Rules 1937, considering all relevant factors,
including the cost of operation, characteristics of service, reasonable profit and the generally prevailing
tariff. The airfares so established are required to be displayed under the provisions of Sub Rule (2) of

21
Rule 135 of Aircraft Rules 1937. Airline remains compliant to the regulatory provisions of Rule 135 as
long as the fare charged by them does not exceed the fare established and displayed on their website.
131. The domestic airline pricing runs in multiple levels (bucket or Reservation Booking Designator
(RBD)) which are in line with the practice followed globally. Usually, the lower levels of the fare in the
fare bucket are assigned to advance purchase (popularly known as Apex Fares) bookings (e.g. up to 90,
60, 30, 14 and 07 days before departure). As time lapses and date of journey approaches closer (from
07 days to date of departure), the fare in higher side of fare bucket are available for purchase. Airline
remains compliant to the regulatory provisions of Rule -135 as long as the fare charged by them does
not exceed the fare established and displayed on their website. In order to prevent excessive charging
and sudden surges in airfares and to promote transparency by scheduled domestic airlines, DGCA has
issued Air Transport Circular 02 of 2010 wherein airlines are required to display on their respective
website the tariff sheet route- wise across their network in various fare categories and the manner it is
offered in the market. The intention behind the above directions is to keep the passengers informed of
pricing pattern of airlines. DGCA has also set up a Tariff Monitoring Unit in 2010 that monitors airfares
on certain routes selected on random basis to ensure that the airlines do not charge airfares outside the
range declared by them.
132. With regard to have maximum retail price on airline tickets, the petition filed with Competition
Commission of India (CCI) in a matter on charges of arbitrary high air fare case No. 68/2012 for issue
of direction to DGCA, Secretary (CA) to fix MRP for airlines, CCI has stated in their order that
Commission cannot give direction to this effect. In fact that will be contrary to the spirit of competition
law. Today, the forces of demand and supply govern the airfares.
Further Recommendations/Observations

CFI/CGI who are the post holders of FTO.

Recommendation/Observation
142. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the number of buggies in all the four metro airports
should be increased according to the requirement of elderly and physically challenged passengers and
buggy services should be made available near the arrival and departure gates to save time. Any
dereliction in this regard should be treated as deficiency of services and violation of OMDA Agreement
and appropriate penalty may be imposed on the airport operator . (Para 80)
Reply of the Government
143. At IGI Airport, buggy services are provided for the movement of persons with reduced mobility,
senior citizens and pregnant women. In addition, buggies are also provided for the movement of dignitaries.
Buggy operations are handled by dedicated vendor who is accountable to service level agreements set
by DIAL. Buggy services are available to passengers on request through the concerned airline, who bears
the primary responsibility to facilitate their passengers; besides having buggy stands at various locations
in the terminal where passengers can place the request directly. Provision of Buggy services is a
voluntary service provided at T3 of the IGI Airport. This is not a stipulated service to be provided under
the terms of the OMDA. Hence any dereliction regarding the Buggy services should not be treated as
deficiency of the services provided by DIAL as violation of OMDA.
Further Recommendations/Observations
144. The Committee notes that any dereliction in providing adequate number of buggies is
against the service level agreements set by DIAL. Therefore, adequate care should be taken to
ensure that enough buggies are made available at the IGI Airport, Delhi.
Recommendation/Observation
145. During the deliberations of the Committee, the Committee learned that there are a large number
of shops in the Delhi airport which are cluttering and encroaching into the public area meant for
passenger amenities. This is also affecting the movement of buggies. The Committee urges upon the
Ministry of Civil Aviation to prevent the Delhi Airport authorities from opening of shops in an unscrupulous
way which are jeopardizing the passenger amenities. (Para 81)
Reply of the Government
146. There has been no encroachment of public spaces meant for passengers of IGI Airport and there
is adequate seating for passengers, movement areas for buggies as well as essential services available
for passengers. ASQ scores achieved by Delhi Airport over the years is a testimony to this.
147. DIAL is guided by OMDA which stipulates that the space for commercial activities at the domestic
and international terminals is allocated as per Section J7.1 of the IATA Airport Development Reference
Manual that has been referred to in the OMDA Schedule 1 (Development Standards and Requirements).
As per IATA Airport Development Reference Manual, in major airports the space for commercial purposes
in a terminal can be used up to 20% whereas in the case of IGI Airport, DIAL has actually used space
for commercial purpose only to the extent to 5.9% of terminal area as against upto 20% standard of

24
IATA. DIAL, from time to time undertakes studies on commercial space allocation based on factors such
as Consumer preference on categories, brands, adjacencies amongst other factors. Space allocation has
been scientifically planned based on such studies. Commercial layout is designed keeping in mind the
objective to fulfil and enhance the passengers experience by ensuring availability of choice of products
and services at the terminals while ensuring utmost comfort and convenience. It is noteworthy that every
retail outlet is provided an approval by BCAS prior to commencement of operations. Passengers flow
and comfort have been given utmost priority.

156. The Committee was informed that the President and Prime Minister of India are eligible for
priority landing and take off in any airports of India whereas the Governors and Chief Ministers are
denied such facilities even in their own States. The Committee observes that Governor and Chief Minister

25
are the Head of State and Head of Government in their respective States and they should get priority
landing rights at par with the President of India and Prime Minister of India. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Ministry of Civil Aviation should modify the relevant rules and regulations to enable
the Governors and Chief Ministers for priority landing in their respective States. (Para 83)

157. Expansion of the list of dignitaries for priority handling of their arrivals and departures at airports
may delay the other aircrafts at airport or in air, which may lead to passenger inconvenience and
congestion at airports and in air. This may also lead to safety concerns at airports and in airspace.
Further, as the Governors and the Chief Ministers of many states travel by scheduled flights also, this
would cause complications in according priority landing/taking off.

Canada is non-existent from the Kolkata airport. A large number of passengers have to go either to Delhi

Report on the issue of preferential treatment given to some airlines (Indigo)
while landing/takeoff:
1 Air Traffic Services are provided to all the airlines as per provisions the provisions of ICAO PAN
ATM Doc 4444 (AAI’s Manual of Air Traffic Services) and National rules/regulations. The approach
sequence is established in a manner which will facilitate arrival of the maximum number of aircraft
with the least average delay. In case of extended delays due to congestion, runway closures/
maintenance, airspace activities etc. the approach sequence is judiciously established on the principle
of accommodating maximum number of aircraft (including departures) irrespective of the airlines,
with least average delay by taking into consideration the total track mileage from touchdown,
respective positions and flight levels, performance profiles etc.
2 Priority is given to:
(a) An aircraft which anticipates being compelled to land because of factors affecting the safe
operation of the aircraft (engine failure, shortage of fuel, etc.);
(b) Hospital aircraft or aircraft carrying any sick or seriously injured person requiring urgent
medical attention;
(c) Aircraft engaged in search and rescue operations; and
(d) VIP I (President), VIP II (Vice President), VIP III (Prime Minister) and VIP V (Foreign
Heads of State/Govt.) aircraft.
3 In order to investigate the issue, two teams, each one comprising of senior Officers, were
constituted at each of six Metro airports (Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Hyderabad and
Bengaluru) which accounts for more than 60% of air traffic in India. One team was required to
monitor traffic pattern and handling of traffic in Aerodrome Control Tower and other team was
required to do the same in Approach Radar Unit for a duration of one hour during peak traffic
hour of that airport.
4 Analysis of reports received from Metro Airports, revealed the following:
(a) During the observation period of one hour of peak traffic at six Metro airports on 06.03.2017,

recommendations as contained in its Two Hundred and Forty Sixth Report on Demands for Grants
(2017-18) of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways which was presented to both the Houses
of Parliament on 17th March, 2017.
2. Action Taken Replies were received from the Government on 19th July, 2017, in respect of all
the observations/recommendations contained in the Report. The replies have been categorized as follows:—
(i) Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
Paragraph Nos.: 6, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 22, 23, 32, 34, 40, 42, 47, 59, 68, 71, 72, 80, 83,
84, 86, 91, 94, 97, 102, 104, 110, 117, 119, 121, 129, 132, 151 and 159 Total: 34
(ii) Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of
the Government replies:-

(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not
been accepted by the Committee:
Paragraph Nos. : 13, 18, 19, 30, 53, 65 and 133 Total: 7
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still
awaited.
Paragraph Nos: 9, 10, 15, 41, 50, 75 and 107 Total: 7

which have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished at the

18. The Ministry/NHAI has taken various steps to stimulate growth and the magnitude of investment
in the road sector.
19. Regular meetings are held with project developers, State Governments and contractors in Head
Quarter by Ministry with Regional Officers, concessionaires/contractors to make the construction of
projects hassle free. To expedite completion of these projects various steps have been taken which
include streamlining of land acquisition and environment clearances, exit for equity investors, premium
re-schedulement, close coordination with other Ministries, revamping of dispute resolution mechanism,
frequent reviews at various levels etc. Further, the Government has taken major initiatives towards
expediting implementation of languishing projects. The various measures taken include :
(a) Environment and Forest Clearance
• Delegation of powers to Regional Offices by Ministry of Environment and Forest.
• EC (Environment Clearance) not required for length of 100 km. Even beyond 100
km. EC is not required if widening is restricted to 40m and realignment to 60m.
(b) ROBs (Rail Over Bridge)/RUBs (Rail Under Bridge):  The procedure for GAD (General
Arrangement Drawing) approved by Railways for ROBs has been simplified and made
online. Maintenance charges which were hampering the progress of many projects, stand
waived by Railways. Standard design have been put on website.

4
(c) Financial initiatives
• Loan secured to the extent of termination payment.
• Infrastructure debt fund - Long term financing at low interest rates
• Re-schedulement of premium - Bank Rate+2%.
• 100% exit after 2 years of completion in projects awarded before 2009.
• Fund infusion by NHAI in stalled projects where the physical progress is 50% and
the concessionaire is facing shortage of funds.
• NHAI liberally permitting refinance with elongation of repayment period. RBI (Reserve
Bank of India) has also issued circular for providing long term debt finance matching
the concession period without classifying the exposure as restructured.
20. With pro-active initiatives, it has been possible to reduce the nos. of languishing projects significantly;
at present, there are only three (3 nos.) of languishing projects.
21. A real time on line monitoring system, “e Samiksha” has been set up by the Cabinet Secretariat
for monitoring of follow up action on the decisions taken during the presentations made by different
Ministries/Departments to the Hon’ble Prime Minister periodically.
22. Also, the portal “PRAGA TI” (pragati.nic.in), i.e. Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation,
has been set up by the Prime Minister’ s Office. The portal is aimed at addressing the Common man’s
grievances and monitoring important programmes and projects. The Hon’ble Prime Minister, himself,
reviews the progress of important infrastructure projects periodically with inputs from the nodal Ministries/
Departments and State Governments, etc., hosted on the Portal. Both these portals, also, discuss the
Centre-Sate Coordination issues within the platform for facilitating better cohesive approach of resolving
the outstanding bottlenecks.
23. In addition to above, at the behest of Prime Minister, a high level Group of Infrastructure has been
constituted under the Chairmanship of Minister of Road Transport and Highways with Ministers of
Railways, Civil Aviation, Minister of State (IC) of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Principal
Secretary to Prime Minister, Cabinet Secretary, Secretary (RT&H), Chairman(Railway Board), Secretary
(Environment and Forests), Secretary(Shipping) and Secretary (Civil Aviation) as Members. The Group
would meet as often required to review and resolve pending Inter-Ministerial matters.

action taken, etc. The progress is centrally monitored in the Ministry, NHAI at the level of concerned
nodal officer and Secretary (RT&H) for facilitating timely redressal at various levels.

the book adjustments of the expenditures regularized with the State AG offices even though works may
have been actually carried out at ground.

195. Total fund of `13717.40 crore was allocated to States/UTs for development of National Highways
under National Highways(Original) and Permanent Bridge Fee Fund Schemes during the year 2016-17.
The payment under the scheme is made by Regional Pay and Accounts Offices (National Highways) after
examination and passing the bills from contractors by Regional Officers of the Ministry under Direct
Payment Procedure(DPP). Hence, Utilisation Certificates for these payment is not required.
196. Fund for development of State Roads are released to States/UTs as “Grant-in-Aid for Creating of

by the State PWDs, are accorded Administrative Approval (AA) by the Ministry as per the extant policy.
Technical Sanction(TS) and Financial concurrence(FS) are given by States. As per the extant policy, one
third of the allocation for the financial year for the State is released for utilisation against sanctioned
works and this amount is maintained as a reserve by replenishing expenditure from subsequent releases.
Further releases of funds during the financial year are made to State based on the utilisation certificates
(UCs) furnished by them.
197. The Ministry while releasing funds to the States based on UCs, etc., duly reviews progress of
works, expenditure incurred on them, etc.

of Delhi to ease the problem faced by the people in negotiating with the large traffic on the road.

200. For ease out of outgoing and gross through traffic coming from outside of Delhi, the NHAI has
taken up construction of about 135 km. long Eastern Peripheral Expressway (EPE). This work is likely
to be completed by this year end. Further, Government of Haryana is also constructing about 135 km.
Western Peripheral Expressway (WPE), which is in continuity of EPE. Both these roads will be a new
Ring Road for about 270 km. around Delhi. All the traffic, which is not bound to Delhi and going to
other places will use this road and this will ease out the traffic in Delhi.
201. On the NH-24, NHAI has started the widening work to the 14-lane NH as a part of Delhi-Meerut
Expressway. The work has been started. On the NH-1, NHAI has started the 8-laning NH work from
Mukaraba Chowk to Delhi border.

31
202. All these NH development work will be helpful to sort out of traffic congestion in and around
Delhi.

204. The Committee is concerned about the increasing number of vehicle and vehicular pollution
caused by them in Delhi. The Committee knows that the Government of Delhi from time-to-time, has
taken steps on the directions of Honorable Courts, to check pollution but the problems of pollution in
Delhi is far from over. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should find out the solution for
vehicular pollution on the roads of Delhi. (Para 132)
Reply of the Government
205. The National Green Tribunal vide its order, dated 18.07.2016 and 20.7.2016 in O.A. 21 of 2014,
Vardhaman Kaushik V/s Union of India has directed that diesel vehicles older than 10 years to be
deregistered in NCR of Delhi. In compliance to the orders of NGT, de-registration of diesel vehicles more
than 10 years old is being carried out by the respective State Government. The proposal to introduce
‘Vehicle Fleet Modernization Programme’ to enable the replacement of Old Vehicles is under consideration.
This will ensure phasing out of older polluting vehicles and enable their replacement with fuel efficient
and environment friendly vehicles. The concept note on ‘Vehicle Fleet Modernization Programme’ to
enable the replacement of Old Heavy and Medium Commercial Vehicles as they contribute the maximum
of vehicular pollution was placed on Ministry’s official website for information and comments from
concerned Ministries and Departments and other stakeholders. The matter has been placed before the
Committee of Secretaries for their recommendations.
206. To reduce vehicular pollution across the country, Government has taken proactive steps to promote
environment friendly vehicles which are innovative, ushering in proactive use of natural resources. Bharat
Stage IV Fuel Norms have been applicable since the year 2010 in Delhi and NCR and certain cities. The
set norms have been mandated in phase-wise manners across the country. The Government has notified
G.S.R. 643(E), dated 19/08/2015 for introduction of BS-IV fuel throughout the country by the year 2017.
Furthermore, steps have been taken by notifying alternate fuels like ethanol, biogas, electric hybrid etc.
by amending the Central Motor Vehicle Rules. Ministry has issued GSR 889(E) dated 16th September,
2016 for introduction of BS VI, mandating mass emission standard for BS-VI throughout the country
w.e.f. from 1st, April 2020.

225. The Ministry is implementing a scheme for providing road safety equipment to States/ UTs for
enforcement. On the basis of requirements received from States during the year 2016-17, financial
assistance was provided to the States of J&K, Sikkim, Punjab and West Bengal. Ministry is inviting
proposals from States/UTs for providing financial assistance for purchase of Breath Analyzers.

identification and rectification of black spots, Road Safety Audits, Road Safety Engineering works on
State Roads under CRF etc. These are circulated to all States/UTs.

CRF amendment rules 2016. Guidelines for implementing these rules have also been issued by the
Ministry.

Safety Annual Plan at a cost of ` 255 crore. Crash barriers have been sanctioned in a length of about
143 km. at a cost of ` 87 crore in hilly terrain on NHs. Capacity building activities through formal and

have participated.

in the country was 
` 6960 crore as GBS and ` 18946.18 crore as IEBR. Out of it, the major chunk of
allocation (GBS) of ` 3902.53 crore was for development of shipping sector and ` 3057.47 crore for
the Port Sector. From the data provided by the Ministry of Shipping, the total allocations made all these
five years was only ` 2306 crores out of which the spending up to 31st January, 2017 is ` 2241.68 crores.
The Committee is very much disappointed to note that the actual allocation made to Ministry of Shipping
is only 32.20% of the outlay (GBS) decided by the Planning Commission. The Committee recommends
that the Ministry of Shipping should give due care in utilizing the allocations promptly by completing
the targeted projects within the stipulated time. (Para 7)

9. At the commencement of the 12th Plan in 2012, the indicative GBS of Ministry of Shipping was
` 6960 crore for the 12th Plan period (2012-17). The actual GBS allocation during the 12th Plan based
on annual budgetary allocations was only Rs 3258.96 crore. The expenditure under GBS upto 31/03/2017
was 3188.92 crore, which is 97.85 % of the total GBS allocations of the Ministry during the 12th plan
period. Thus, the Ministry had utilized almost the complete plan funds provided to it as per the budgetary
allocations. It may be appreciated that Ministry of Finance undertakes the budgetary allocations across
Ministries/Departments/States depending on the overall priorities of the Government.
Further Recommendation/Observation
10. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
11. The Committee desires to know the comparison of the targets fixed by the erstwhile Planning
Commission during 12th Plan period for the Ministry of Shipping and the achievements of the targets
made by the Ministry at the end of the 12th Plan period. The year wise details and the percentage of
achievement, etc. of each of the targets set in the Port and Shipping Sectors may be provided at the time
of submission of the Action Taken Replies to this report. (Para 8)
Reply of the Government
PORTS SECTOR
12. The position with reference to the targets envisaged in the 12th Plan for the Ports Wing is as
under:

3
(a) Traffic and Capacity Augmentation: The 12thPlan projected total capacity of the port
sector to be 2,289.04 million tonnes (1,229.24 MT - Major Ports and 1,059.80 MT.- non-
Major Ports) and over all traffic of the ports to be 1,758.26 MT (943.06 MT. - Major Ports
and 815.20 MT. -Non Major Ports) by 2016-17. The total installed capacity of the Indian
Ports at the end of the 12th Plan was 1897.11 MT (1065.83MT -Major Ports, 831.28 MT
- Non Major Ports) as on 31st March 2017 compared to 1245.30 MT (696.53 MT Major
Ports, 548.77 MT Non Major Ports) at the end of 11th plan. The traffic handled by the
Ports at the end of the 12th Plan has been 1135.76 MT (647.76 MT Major Ports, 488 MT
Non Major Ports) as on 31st March 2017 compared to 913.32 MT (560.14 MT Major
Ports, 353.18 MT Non Major Ports) at the end of the 11th plan. The year wise details
pertaining to Capacity and traffic handled at Major Ports are as under:

(b) Dredging: The 12th plan envisaged to increase the drafts to at least 14 meters in all ports
by the end of 12th plan period and achieve 17 meters in Hub-Ports. 10 of the Major Ports
have already achieved a draft of 14 meters or more.
(c) Productivity and Dwell Time: As emphasized in the 12th Plan, successful attempts have
already been initiated for closely working with Customs Department to reduce the dwell
time for containers in Ports and CFSs. Also, Direct Port Delivery facility, under the accredited
client programme has been extended by JNPT.
(d) Containerization and Hinterland Connectivity.: The share of Containerized traffic during
2016-17 was 19.23%. The container handling capacity of Major Ports increased from
138.88 Million Tonnes during 2011-12 to 183.81 Million Tonnes during 2016-17 with a
CAGR of 5.92%. Due focus was given in Twelfth Plan for increasing the share of
containerized cargo in ports with a view to capturing a higher share of international trade.
A number of projects for rail/road connectivity were taken up and monitored closely both
for Major and non-Major Ports.
(e) Private Sector Participation: In the 12th Plan, the need for working out PPP model for
infrastructure Port development Project was stressed. Active steps have been taken to fully
utilize the potential, resources and professionalism of the private sector. These include

implementation/construction.
(f) Development of Non Major Ports: The share of capacity creation at the Indian Ports is
constantly increasing. It has increased from 39% during 2011-12 to 43% during 2016-17.

Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra etc.

revenues. In addition, revenues were reduced due to scheduled dry docking of the vessels.

to treat pollutants of ships and terminals through STPs. Necessary provisions have been kept in the
amendments proposed to the Inland Vessels Act 1917, to contain sewage, oil leakages and other effluents

suggestion will be considered after the Inland Vessel Rules are framed based on the new Inland Waterways

155. India is a party to International Convention on Prevention of Pollution at sea by ships (MARPOL
73/78) and other relevant convention applicable for prevention of marine pollution incidents. National
Legislation is in place to control and prevent pollution incidient caused by ships registered under Merchant
Shipping Act, 1958 and foreign flag vessels visiting Indian Ports. National laws/rules give the effect of
International Convection through the provisions made in Merchant Shipping Act, 1958, towards mitigation,
containment/control, removal or combat of oil spillage, whether accidental or otherwise. The Merchant
Shipping Prevention of Pollution Rule and formulation of contingency plan give effect to international
convention in order to take action consequent to any spillage incident whether accidental or otherwise,
the same can be dealt with.
156. Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP) and Shipboard Marine Pollution Emergency Plan
(SMPEP) or Vessels Response Plan or Garbage Management Plan or other plans, as applicable, are
maintained on board the ships to prevent and contain oil pollution incidents.
157. Indian and foreign flag ships are inspected at Indian ports under Flag State and Port State control
regime, so as to make sure that preventive measures on ships are in conformity to relevant international
convention.
158. National Oil Spill Disaster Contingency Plan is being maintained to undertake oil spill prevention
and control measures. Lesson learnt are shared among the authorities/stakeholders and to update the plan
periodically.
159. The authorities in the major ports co-ordinate with the other local action groups as per requirements.
All major ports have been notified to have oil/garbage reception facilities as required by the Convention.
160. Accordingly, the pollution incidents are handled and control measures are taken to prevent pollution
under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan on these set mechanisms.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
recommendations/observations as contained in its Two Hundred and Forty Fifth Report on
Demands for Grants (2017-18) of the Ministry of Culture which was presented to both the Houses
of Parliament on 17 th March, 2017.
2. Action Taken Replies were received from the Government on 27 th July, 2017, in respect of all the
recommendations/observations contained in the Report. The replies have been categorized as follows:–
(i) Recommendations/Observations that have been accepted by the Government:
Paragraph Nos.: 7, 16, 38 , 57, 92, 95, 98, 106, and 113 Total: 9
(ii) Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the
Government replies:
Paragraph Nos.: 28 and 31 Total: 2
(iii) Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been
accepted by the Committee:
Paragraph Nos. : 22, 25, 34, 42, 51, 77, 86, 89, 110, 117 and 121 T otal: 11
(iv) Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still
awaited.
Paragraph Nos: 10, 19, 45, 48, 65, 68, 80 and 101 Total: 8
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of those recommendations/observations
which have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished at the earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of Action
Taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the Committee contained in the Two
Hundred and Forty Fifth Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry and recommendations/observations of
the Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs:
Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee notes that the budgetary allocation for 2017-18 is about 10.04% more than the budgetary
provisions at RE 2016-17. The Committee is surprised to note that the Ministry had to face a budgetary
reduction at RE stage in the previous financial year. The Committee would like to know the reasons for the
same.
(Para 10)
Reply of the Government
6. As against total budgetary provision of  ` 2500.00 crore at Budget Estimates (BE) 2016-17 which was
reduced to ` 2488.63 crore at Revised Estimates (RE) stage 2016-17, the budget for 2017-18 for Ministry
of Culture has been pegged at  ` 2738.47 crore. Ministry of Finance has not intimated any reason for the
reduction in Annual Plan allocation at RE stage during 2016-17. However, the Ministry will make efforts to
seek an additional allocation at RE stage during the current financial year 2017-18.

2
Further Recommendations/Observations
7. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
8. The Committee notes that the shortfall in budgetary allocation for 2017-18 is to the tune of
 ` 828.24
crore and that the Ministry of Finance has not intimated any reason for this reduction. Keeping in view the
crucial role played by culture in the Nation’s overall development and growth, the Committee is of the
considered view that with the present allocation, especially on the Capital side, it would be difficult to run
the existing schemes and other activities undertaken by the Ministry. Therefore, the Committee recommends
that the Ministry should actively pursue the matter of increasing the allocation at the RE stage in the current
financial year 2017-18, with the Ministry of Finance.
(Para 13)
Reply of the Government
9. The Ministry will take up the issue for providing additional funds with Ministry of Finance at RE stage
in the current financial year 2017-18.
Further Recommendations/Observations
10. The Committee may be apprised of the outcome thereof.
Recommendation/Observation
11. The Committee takes note of the expenditure made by the Ministry of Culture under the Plan and Non
Plan heads. At the same time, the Committee observes that under the Plan head for the financial years
2015-16 and 2016-17, better planning and supervision could have definitely improved the pace of utilization
and for achievement of set target. The Committee hopes that optimum pace of expenditure would be maintained
in future.
(Para 17)
Reply of the Government
12. The Ministry will continue to make all out efforts for optimizing the utilization of allocated funds
during the year 2017-18.
Further Recommendations/Observations
13. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
14. In this regard, the Committee impresses upon the Ministry that every possible step should be taken to
ensure that the stipulated outputs are achieved on time.
(Para 19)
Reply of the Government
15. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. The Ministry has prepared the output/outcome
targets under all schemes which are being monitored by the Ministry as well as NITI Aayog. Moreover,
Ministry signs Memorandum of Understandings (MoUs) with its organizations in which specific targets of

3
work are assigned. The achievements against the targets are monitored on regular basis at the appropriate
level.
Further Recommendations/Observations
16. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
17. The Committee recommends that an Inquiry Committee may be constituted to look into the facts and
circumstances which led to the delay in construction of the Institute of Archaeology. Based on the findings,
action may be taken against those officials found guilty and a report in this regard may be submitted to the
Committee. The Committee strongly recommends that effective and periodic monitoring of the various
Organizations under the Ministry should be done in order to avoid such delays.
(Para 22)
Reply of the Government
18. Ministry of Culture had in November, 2013 called for a thorough inquiry into the cancellation of plot
allotted by Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority (GNIDA) to Archaeological Survey of India
(ASI) for setting up of Institute of Archaeology and to fix responsibility of the officers responsible for the
same. Accordingly, a thorough examination of the progression of this proposal was conducted and a detailed
factual report was submitted chronologically by ASI to the Ministry of Culture for consideration and further
directions. The factual report in this regard was considered in the Ministry at the level of Hon’ble Culture
Minister. Thereafter, the matter with regard to restoration of the plot was taken up at the level of Secretary
(Culture) with the Govt. of U.P. and CEO, GNIDA. After vigorously pursuing the case, the plot has been
restored to ASI after fulfilling the conditions laid down by GNIDA. Further action for construction of the
building for Institute of Archaeology has been initiated after obtaining the approval of the Delegated Investment
Board (DIB). The work is being executed by National Buildings Construction Corporation (NBCC) and as
per the schedule of construction, the work is likely to be completed by July, 2019. The Project Monitoring
Committee is also constituted to monitor the progress of the projects. Further, periodic review meetings are
taken by the higher authorities in the Ministry to monitor the various organizations and MoUs signed by the
Ministry with them.
Further Recommendations/Observations
19. The Committee may be apprised about the progress of construction of the Institute of
Archaeology along with the names of the officers responsible for monitoring the construction. The
Committee further recommends that the Ministry should ensure that target is achieved within the
stipulated time.
Recommendation/Observation
20. The Committee welcomes the initiative taken to construct boundary walls for ASI protected monuments.
The Committee hopes that this will go a long way in preventing encroachment of monuments. The Committee
desires that a roadmap may be drawn for the construction of boundary walls for all the ASI protected
monuments and that existing timelines may be strictly adhered to. The Committee may be informed of the
progress made in the matter.
(Para 27)

4
Reply of the Government
21. The work for construction of boundary walls and toilet blocks at ASI protected monuments has been
assigned to Telecommunications Consultants India Limited (TCIL) and Water and Power Consultancy Services
(WAPCOS), the Government of India undertakings. Most of the estimates for construction of boundary
walls have been approved for which tenders have been initiated by the concerned agencies and the work is
in progress at some sites. The work order for some of the sites have been issued. M/s. TCIL & W APCOS
shall be instructed to ensure the time line of work orders.
Further Recommendations/Observations
22. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should take necessary measures to
expedite the work and ensure that progress of work is not stalled at any stage. The Committee may
be apprised of the achievements in physical terms.
Recommendation/Observation
23. The Committee is unhappy to note the non-implementation of e-Governance in ASI. The Committee is
of the view that in this era of rapid advancement in technology, it is essential that e-Governance is adopted
in a vital Organization like ASI. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take proactive steps to
ensure that e-Governance is implemented in ASI. The Committee may be apprised of the action taken in this
regard.
(Para 29)
Reply of the Government
24. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has given all necessary approval with regard to development/
design of necessary software for implementation of e-governance in ASI.
Further Recommendations/Observations
25. The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Culture and ASI has not given any
details of the e-governance projects they are planning to implement. The Committee notes that the
authorities have taken some initiatives only after this Committee has come down heavily on the
inaction of the ASI to implement e-governance initiatives. The Committee recommends that the
Ministry should follow up the progress of development of necessary software for implementation of
e-governance in ASI and ensure that the implementation of e-governance in ASI is expedited. The
Committee may be apprised about the details and progress of implementation of e-governance
projects.
Recommendation/Observation
26. The Committee observes that e-ticketing enables the visitors to plan their visit to the monuments in
advance and help them to avoid the hassle of waiting at the ticket counters. Therefore, the Committee
desires that the facility of e-ticketing may be introduced in all ASI protected monuments.
(Para 31)
Reply of the Government
27. The online e-ticketing facility has already been introduced in all centrally protected ticketed monuments
of Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

5
Further Recommendations/Observations
28. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
29. The Committee appreciates the initiative taken by the Department and hopes that the App would not
only ensure greater accountability of the concerned agencies but also ensure a clean environment around the
Centrally Protected Monuments.
(Para 33)
Reply of the Government
30. With regard to ‘Swatchh Paryatan Mobile App’, the responsibility of ASI is to redress the issue raised
on the above App. As and when any complaint is received, the same is being immediately addressed by the
respective nodal officers of ASI designated for this purpose.
Further Recommendations/Observations
31. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
32. The Committee welcomes the initiatives taken under Adarsh Smarak and desires that such improved
facilities may be provided in all the ASI monuments in a phased manner.
(Para 35)
Reply of the Government
33. With regard to the recommendation of the Committee contained in para 35, the suggestion and
observations suggested by the Committee are welcome. In this regard, it is pertinent to mention that in
spite of 25 Adarsh Monuments, ASI has already identified 75 monuments and Sites as Adarsh Monument
in second phase where tourist amenities such as drinking water, cafeteria, wi-fi, souvenir shop, Audio
Video centre and facilities for disabled may be provided. Out of the 100 Adarsh monuments 56 monuments
are ticketed while 44 monuments are not-ticketed. With regard to suggestions made by the Committee, it
is to mention that all ASI protected monuments and sites are not frequently visited by the tourists. Most
of the protected monuments in ASI are not being visited even by a single tourist. Therefore, the extension
of the facilities for all monuments in phased manner as suggested by the Committee does not seem
feasible as well as economical. In this regard it is proposed that the Circle Offices of ASI may be directed
to identify at least 5 monuments under their jurisdiction for upgrading amenities as suggested by the
Committee.
Further Recommendations/Observations
34. The Committee recommends that a feasibility study may be conducted by ASI on identifying
the Monuments which have the potential to be declared as Adarsh Monuments and the results of
the study may be communicated to the Committee.
Recommendation/Observation
35. As per the Annual Report of the Ministry, in 2016-17 ASI created two new Circles at Aizawl and
Telangana.
(Para 36)

6
36. The Committee desires to know the budgetary allocation earmarked for the purpose.
(Para 37)
Reply of the Government
37. The budgetary allocation in respect of Aizawl Circle and Telangana / Hyderabad Circle during the year
2016-17 was ` 162.64 lakhs and ` 2092.00 lakhs respectively.
Further Recommendations/Observations
38. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
39. The Ministry, in its written reply, has stated that nine and twenty-eight Demolition Orders have been
issued by the Archaeological Survey of India so far for the removal of unauthorized construction within the
prohibited/regulated areas of Zaffar Mahal and Qutub complex respectively.
(Para 38)
40. The Committee desires that ASI should ensure that the demolition orders are executed timely and that
the encroachments are removed.
(Para 39)
Reply of the Government
41. Demolition orders are being issued properly as and when cases of encroachments are reported. However,
the field officers of ASI may please be directed to keep regular visit and take appropriate response/ action
against the person as per provisions of The Ancient Monument and Archaeological Sites and Remains
(AMASR) Act, 1958 and Rules, 1959 and the eviction of unauthorized property for Public Premises (Eviction
of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971.
Further Recommendations/Observations
42. The Committee is not convinced by the reply of the Ministry. The Committee desires that the
Ministry should ensure that the field officers of ASI take appropriate action against the encroachers.
The Committee would like to know the number of encroachment eviction orders issued during the
last three years and the results thereof.
Recommendation/Observation
43. In response to a pointed query as to whether legal opinion has been received from the Ministry of Law
on the powers of ASI for demolition with regard to action on District Authorities in case of laxity or non-co-
operation on their part in executing the demolition order, the Ministry has replied that legal opinion is being
sought. The Committee recommends that this process of seeking legal opinion may be expedited so that
further course of action can be taken with regard to District Authorities.
(Para 41)
Reply of the Government
44. The suggestion of the Committee has been considered and engagement of Legal Consultant at the
Circle level is being considered to expedite the cases with regard to encroachment and illegal/unauthorized
construction.

7
Further Recommendations/Observations
45. The Committee may be apprised of the outcome thereof.
Recommendation/Observation
46. The Committee emphasizes the need for greater co-ordination between ASI and the State Governments
in the matter of prevention and removal of encroachments at the monuments. The Committee impresses
upon the Ministry to persuade the State Governments to form State level Co-ordination Committees for
prevention and removal of encroachments at the monuments. The Committee also recommends that a
separate wing may be created within the Ministry of Culture and ASI to oversee the removal of encroachments
in an effective way.
(Para 42)
Reply of the Government
47. It is proposed that the SA’s/Dy. SA’s of Circles/Mini Circles would be directed to co-ordinate with
State Authorities responsible for removal of encroachments from protected monuments. Formulation
of a Co-ordination Committee is under consideration in every State at higher level for addressing the
issues.
Further Recommendations/Observations
48. The Committee may be informed of the outcome thereof.
Recommendation/Observation
49. The Committee notes that the Ministry and ASI, New Delhi has stock of information on removal of
encroachment of only three circles. This shows the lackadaisical attitude of the Ministry and ASI towards
removal of encroachments. The Committee is aware of the fact that a large number of monuments are
encroached and many of them are with active connivance of anti-social elements. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that they should obtain quarterly report of the progress made from each of the circles regarding
removal of encroachments. The Committee may be apprised about the status of removal of encroachment
from all the circles of ASI in the Action taken Report.
(Para 44)
Reply of the Government
50. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has prepared a data bank with regard to encroachment
already taken place inside the protected monuments/sites. The data with regard to removal of encroachment
during the last three years is being prepared and to be submitted in a Parliament Assurance reply. The
suggestion of the Committee with regard to obtaining quarterly report of the progress from each circle is
welcomed and all SA’s/Dy. SA’s of Circles/Mini circle would be directed to submit the Action Taken Report
as desired by the Committee.
Further Recommendations/Observations
51. The Committee notes with utter dismay that even after six months the Government has not
submitted any quarterly report on encroachment to the Committee. It seems that the
recommendations of the Committee are taken lightly. No concrete action has been taken on a very

8
important issue. The Committee would like to know the names of the officers of the Ministry
responsible for supply of the information as recommended by the Committee and the action taken
against them for non supply of information as recommended by the Committee.
Recommendation/Observation
52. The Committee desires that the Ministry may take up with the Ministry of Finance, the need for
enhancement under the Capital head at the RE stage.
(Para 46)
Reply of the Government
53. The Delegated Investment Board (DIB) meeting held on 28.3.2017 under the Chairmanship of Secretary,
Ministry of Culture has approved the proposal for construction of Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of
Archaeology at Greater Noida out of the commemoration budget subject to relaxation of GFR provisions by
the Ministry of Finance. It was also decided that up to 30% of the cost of the project may be considered for
release to National Buildings Construction Corporation (NBCC) during the financial year 2016-17 after
adjusting the 10 crores already released by ASI. During the above meeting, the participants were informed
that the project is likely to be completed in 24 months from the date of its start.
54. The likely date of start is 1st June 2017 and the project is likely to be completed by 31st May, 2019.
The period of 24 months will fall in three financial years viz. 2017-18, 2018-19 and 2019-20.

was ` 22800 crore. Out of it, the major chunk of allocation of ` 9450 crore was for development of

and desires to know the details of the reasons why such huge difference occurred in allocations to the tourism
sector during 12th Five Year Plan in the country.

11. The Committee notes the confidence shown by the Secretary, Tourism that by the end of the financial
year they would be able to spend the revised allocation of ` 1599.03 crore during 2016-17. The Committee,
however, notes that under the Head Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure even 50% of
the allocation out of the 
` 70 crore has not been made so far. This trend can be seen also in the restructured
scheme of Overseas Promotion and Publicity including MDA where, out of the r evised allocation of
` 223.00 crore, the amount spent so far is ` 91.26 crore only. In case of North East Region, all the heads are
showing zero spending. The Committee is constrained to understand how the Ministry of Tourism is able to
spend the entire allocation within a period of two months time as claimed by the Secretary, Tourism. The
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should be more pragmatic in their approach in
implementing the schemes and spending of allocation so that the sanctions could be utilized systematically
