progress to rectify the bugs and make the system operational. This seriously hampered the system
to go live.
17.2. The matter was accordingly, taken up with CMD, ECIL to resolve the impediments in order
to ensure successful launch of the project in a stipulated timeframe. Also, the matter was taken
up with Department of Atomic Energy through MoCA.
17.3. As result of rigorous follow-up, ECIL communicated on 2/5/2018. ECIL reconstituted it’s
technical team. This team started working on the development of application in May-2018. Currently,
application has been deployed at the Data Center by ECIL and is being assessed and tested by the
stakeholders (Airports). ECIL is working to fix all bugs as reported in the last User acceptance test.
Currently, ECIL is preparing the load testing prerequisites with their technology partner‘s (IBM).
The impediments/issues found during test are expected to be rectified by end of June, 2018.
However, the same could not be fixed by ECIL.
17.4. To expedite the implementation of project, a meeting was held on 06.07.2018 under Chairmanship
of DG , BCAS. In the meeting, ECIL has informed that the load testing of software is likely to
complete by 14
th Aug 2018, which will be followed by bug fixing, if any. Thereafter, the system
would Go-Live for the pass printing activity.

3. The Committee, in its earlier Reports, had recommended that the Ministry should take effective

Reply of the Ministry
3.1. W ith the repeal of Air Corporation Act in March 1994, the process of airfare approval by
Government has been dispensed with. As per prevailing regulation, airfares are not regulated by the
Government. Under the provision of Sub Rule (1) of Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 1937, every
air transport undertaking engaged in scheduled air services require to establish tariff having regard
to all relevant factors, including cost of operation, characteristic of services, reasonable profit and
the generally prevailing tariff. Airlines are free to charge reasonable airfares as per their operation
viabilities subject to compliance to above said rule. The airline pricing system runs in multiple levels
(buckets of RBDs) which are in line with practice being followed globally. The prices are fixed
by airlines keeping in mind the market, demand, seasonality and other market forces. The airfare
increases with increases in demand of seat as the lower fare buckets get sold out fast when
bookings are offered by airlines. Some of the airlines have introduced advance purchase schemes
of 90 days, 60 days, 30 days, 14 days etc.., wherein highly discounted fares are offered which
would entail travelling even during peak seasons on low fares. The fare structures are displayed
by airlines on their websites under the provision of Sub Rule (2) of Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules,
1937. The airlines remain compliant to the prevailing regulation as long as fares charged by them
are in line with fare displayed on their website. Further, DGCA monitors airfares on certain routes
selected on random basis to ensure that the airlines do not charge airfares outside the range
declared by them. The analysis has shown that the airfares remain well within the fare bucket
uploaded by the airlines on the respective websites.
3.2. Competition Commission of India (CCI) in its order dated 06/03/2012 on fixing of MRP for
airfares has stated, CCI cannot give direction to the Government to fix MRP of a service provided

25
by private entrepreneur and that the same will be contrary to the spirit of the competition law. CCI
also stated that the forces of demand and supply govern airfares.

containing the surge in airfares and the resultant profiteering by different airlines. The

prevail upon different Airlines not only to make available more and more low-fare bucket
seats but also to keep the airfares at reasonably affordable level. The Committee strongly
feels that an upper cap of airfare in each Sector is the need of the hour to discourage the
Airlines from predatory pricing of air tickets.

Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee notes that there has been a huge jump in the number of aircrafts used for

of dues from Kingfisher Airlines and take urgent legal steps for recovery thereof.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV A TIONS  —  AT A GLANCE
CHAPTER-III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF
THE MINISTRY HA VE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
The Ministry in its Action Taken Replies submitted in the year 2016 on 238 th report of
the Committee had furnished the same word-to-word reply against the recommendation of
the Committee. As still the Ministry has failed to recover its outstanding dues, the above
measures seem not to be effective. The Ministry & AAI should tighten their approach and
legal action may be initiated in appropriate cases besides withholding necessary permission
and cancellation of licences, etc. The Committee desires that the Ministry/AAI shall explore
other penal measures, such as not granting requisite permissions, cancellation of licences,
etc. for recovery of outstanding dues. (Para 1.2)
The reply does not reflect the views expressed by the Committee or the current
scenario in so far as recruitment for senior level positions in BCAS is concerned. The
Ministry should be categorical to ensure that due consideration is extended to cadre officials
rather than deputationists in filling up senior level management positions. The Committee
may be apprised about the timelines proposed for the restructuring of BCAS and the
schedule of implementation. (Para 2.2)
The reply does not reflect the seriousness of the efforts made by the Ministry in
containing the surge in airfares and the resultant profiteering by different airlines. The
Committee feels that concerted efforts should be consistently made by the Ministry to
prevail upon different Airlines not only to make available more and more low-fare bucket
seats but also to keep the airfares at reasonably affordable level. The Committee strongly
feels that an upper cap of airfare in each Sector is the need of the hour to discourage the
Airlines from predatory pricing of air tickets. (Para 3.3)
The Committee reiterates that concerted efforts should be made to ensure that the
Airlines consistently increase the low-fare bucket seats to facilitate the common man to opt
for air travel. With every long weekend and vacation in sight, air fares are increased
manifold. Even during natural calamities, people are not spared to pay extremely higher
fares. The Committee also feels that till the time ATF is not included under GST, a system
may be developed to automatically pass the benefits to the consumers whenever ATF prices
are decreased. (Para 4.3)
The Committee feels that the DGCA and the AAI should encourage setting up of new
FTOs and ensure smooth operation of existing FTOs by providing necessary infrastructure
and reducing the fee charged from them. The Committee calls upon the Government to see
the sluggishness in Flight Training Organisations in India. For any industry to survive, the
critical subsystems which support it should also grow and flourish along with the main
industry; if not the growth of 20% in Aviation may be short-lived. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Government should give all the encouragement for the FTOs to
grow. (Para 5.4)

proactive in tackling the issue of shortage of trained Pilots and take urgent steps to
have sufficient number of trained indigenous pilots and reduce dependence on foreign
pilots. (Para 6.2)

on Demands for Grants (2018-19) of the Ministry of Culture which was presented to both the

THE MINISTRY 
 
MINISTRY’S PROJECTED DEMAND vis-à-vis Budgetary Allocation 
 
1. The Committee notes that the budgetary allocation for 2018 -19 has been marginally 
increased by 3.83% more than the budgeta ry provisions at BE 2017 -18 which is not an 
increase at all considering the inflation. This Committee is unhappy to note that Culture has 
not been given due attention and totally ignored by the Government. The allocated amount is 
short by Rs. 999.7 crore a gainst the projected amount. The Committee was informed by the 
Ministry that due to the cut in the allocation the functioning of ASI and various museums may 
be affected. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should pursue for an increase in 
budget allocation during RE 2018 -19 as the activities undertaken by the Ministry of Culture 
are very crucial in maintaining the cultural identity of the nation by highlighting and 
preserving its rich cultural heritage.           
 (Para 11 of the 258th Report) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 Efforts will be made by the Ministry to get the allocation enhanced at RE 2018 -19 to 
undertake the activities of the Ministry which have been adversely effected due to marginal 
increase of Budgetary allocation at BE 2018-19. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
1.2 The Committee notes the reply.

ticketing facility in ASI protected ticketed monuments and museums as it makes it convenient 
for visitors to plan their visit to the monuments in advance and help them to avoid the hassle 
of waiting at the ticket counters. The Committee desires that the facility of e -ticketing may be 
introduced in the remaining ASI protected monuments as well.

remaining protected monuments has been followed for implementation.

regard.

Recommendation/Observation
9. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take initiative to encourage private
participation in various road projects. (Para 30)
Reply of the Ministry
9.1 Private investment in road infrastructure through PPP route was on decline because the
traditional Build Operate Transfer (BOT) model had high traffic and capital risk for the private
player which made it unattractive. As a result, the Government has implemented the Hybrid Annuity
Model (HAM) wherein 40% of the upfront investment is borne by the Government and the private
partner gets guaranteed annuities over a 15 year period. Toll is collected by the Government which
thus takes over the entire traffic risk. Government, on the other hand is able to stagger its capital
investment over a longer 15 year period as opposed to the traditional EPC project. The Ministry/
NHAI has been awarding projects under Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM)/Built-operate-Transfer (BOT)
and has awarded 15% length in 2015-16; 17% length in 2016-17; 21% length in 2017-18 under
HAM/BOT mode out of the total awarded length.
9.2 NHAI has also launched Masala Bonds which is rupee denominated bonds issued in a foreign
country. These have been able to attract foreign investment and address currency fluctuation risk
which otherwise required additional hedging costs.
9.3 Further, as already mentioned in reply to para 15 ante, CCEA approved Toll, Operate and
Transfer (TOT) Model in August, 2016 for monetisation of developed NH stretches; it is targeted
to raise funds to the tune of about ` 34,000 crore under TOT concessions upto 2021-22. Target
of ` 20,000 crore has been set for realization of funds under TOT during 2018-19; this includes
first bu ndle of TOT concessions awarded for 9 nos. of NH stretches of 680 km. length for

Bid Concession Fee of ` 9,681.50 crore, for which fund is expected to be realised during
2018-19.

important for the creation and maintenance of road projects in a vast country like India.

10. The Committee recommends that issues regarding land acquisition and Environment/ Forest/
Wildlife Clearance should be planned well in advance to avoid delay if taken up at a later stage
as one cannot predict the minor details involved in each project. (Para 34)
Reply of the Ministry
10.1 The Projects are awarded after adequate progress is achieved in terms of Land Acquisition,
obtaining statutory clearances, etc. The process for which is initiated after finalisation of alignment
and submission of final feasibility report by the Consultant.
10.2 The process of land acquisition and securing clearances are initiated during the process of
project preparation. The processes have been streamlined to a great extent. Regarding Environment
and Forest Clearances, MoEF&CC has delegated powers to their Regional Offices to cut short the
delay. Also, permission for felling of the tree is given by the forest department after Stage-I
clearance only without waiting for Stage-II clearance subject to further deposition of amount of
Net Present V alue (NPV) and Compensatory Afforestation (CA) as decided by the Forest Department.
10.3 Multiple initiatives have been identified and undertaken to streamline and expedite land acquisition
process and simplify procedures. Firstly, the entire process of preparation and issuance of land
acquisition notifications has been moved to an online system known as Bhoomi Rashi. Under this,
the draft notification is prepared by the CALA (Competent Authority Land Acquisition) and the
Project Director (PD) and all the approvals, at regional level and at central level such as at NHAI
headquarters or at Ministry, are obtained through the online workflows. This has ensured swift
processing, eliminated discrepancies such as those between multiple versions of notification, and
has ensured transparency of where approvals are pending. It has thus been possible to reduce the
entire process of preparation and approval from an earlier approximate 3 months to 7-10 days.
10.4 Further, to expedite land acquisition at the end of CALA, DPR consultant has now been made
responsible for assisting in preparation and approval of land acquisition notifications, including
providing necessary support to CALA to assist in on-ground surveys.
10.5 Also, Special Land Acquisition Units (SLAUs) have been set up in identified states. These are
special LA units headed by CALA from the district administration and staffed with dedicated
officials from Ministry or NHAI such that the special unit is able to focus on LA for highway and
road projects.
10.6 Additionally, the process of review and approval of award under 3G has been delegated to
various Regional Officers (RO) of NHAI. The approval can now be accorded at field level in most

11
of the situations instead of referring the same to head office level thereby reducing the time
involved in finalization of awards.
10.7 For streamlining LA under NH Act, 1956 and applicability of the Right to Fair Compensation
and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act 2013 for
LA of NH projects, the Ministry has issued comprehensive guidelines on 28.12.2017 detailing the
current procedures and practices in supersession of all previous guidelines/ circulars on the issue
after obtaining legal advice from learned Attorney General of India. These guidelines have been
circulated to all State /UT Governments and all concerned executive agencies of the Ministry. These
guidelines cover all possible aspects related to applicability of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 to the NH
Act, 1956, determination of market value of land, payment of additional amount, issue regarding
multiplication factor, bulk acquisition/ purchase of land through consent of land owners, determination
of compensation amount by competent authority, disbursement of compensation amount and possession
of land, etc.
Further Recommendation/Observation

SWACHCHTA ACTION PLAN
Recommendation/Observation
24. The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry has taken initiatives to adopt Swachchta

24.1 Currently, roads in India lack structured wayside amenities like clean toilets, hygienic restaurants/

even if available, do not meet the diverse requirements of different classes of road users -like car

and heavy vehicle drivers, Type -2 facility targeting passengers only and Type -3 facility targeting
truck drivers only.

having minimum land area of more than 2 Ha abutting the National Highways can join hands with
NHAl under the brand name called “Highway Nest” for development of wayside amenities as a co-
branding partnership with the authority. The private land owners/entrepreneurs shall be developing
the facilities as per standard layouts and designs of NHAI and co-branding with NHAI as “Highway
Nest”. The private land owners/entrepreneurs shall be assisted in providing free access permission

a service level agreement with NHAI.

Recommendation/Observation

26
System, passenger services, data analysis, induction of electric vehicles, introduction of technology,

Recommendation/Observation

the Ministry should take necessary steps to ensure that the allocated amount is utilized fully.

at the RE stage in the five Annual Plans. (Para 8)

2.1. Noted.

2.2. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
3. The Committee desire to know the comparison of the targets fixed by the erstwhile Planning
Commission during 12th Plan periodfor the Ministry of Shipping and the achievements of the targets
made by the Ministry at the end of the 12th Plan period. The year wise details and the percentage of
achievement etc. of each of the targets set in the Port and Shipping Sectors may be provided at the time
of submission of Action Taken Replies to this Report. The Committee notes that the trend of not utilizing
the allocated fund for various programmers in all the five years of the 12th Plan period is a bad
management and inefficiency on the part of the Ministry of Shipping. The BE got reduced sustainably
at RE levels during the Plan period and this definitely shows the Ministry in poor light. The Committee
may be informed about the steps taken by the Ministry to utilize the allocated fund effectively in future.
(Para 9)
Reply of the Government
3.1. The position with reference to the targets envisaged in the 12th Plan for the Ports Wing is as under:
(i) Traffic and Capacity Augmentation: The 12t Plan projected total capacity of the port sector
to be 2,289.04 million tonnes (1,229.24 MT - Major Ports and 1,059.80 MT.- non-Major
2

3
Ports) and over all traffic of the ports to be 1,758.26 MT (943.06 MT. - Major Ports and
815.20 MT. - Non Major Ports) By 2016-17. The total installed capacity of the Indian Ports
at the end of the 12th Plan was 2161.85 MT (1359 MTMajor Ports, 802.85 MT - Non Major
Ports) as on 31 March 2017 compared to 1245.30 MT (696.53 MT Major Ports, 548.77 MT
Non Major Ports) at the end of 11th plan. The traffic handled by the Ports at the end of the
12th Plan has been 1133.61 MT (648.40 MT Major Ports, 485.21 MT Non Major Ports) as
on 31st March 2017 compared to 913.32 MT (560.14 MT Major Ports, 353.18 MT Non
Major Ports) at the end of the 11th plan.
(ii) Dredging: The 12th Plan highlighted that drafts at Indian ports both in the channel and at
berths need to be improved. Objective should be to increase the drafts to at least 14 meters
in all ports by the end of 12th plan period and achieve 17 meters in Hub-Ports. 10 of the Major
Ports have already achieved a draft of 14 meters or more. Some of the ports like Mormugao,
Kamarajar (Ennore), have place to achieve much higher drafts.
(iii) Productivity and Dwell Time: As emphasized in the 12thPlan, successful attempts have already
been initiated for closely working with Customs Department to reduce the dwell time for
containers in Ports and CFSs. Also Direct Port Delivery facility, under the accredited client
programme has been extended by JNPT.
(iv) Containerization and Hinterland Connectivity.: The share of Containerized traffic during 2016-
17 was 19.23%. The container handling capacity of Major Ports increased from 138.88 Million
Tonnes during 2011-12 to 183.81 Million Tonnes during 2016-17 with a CAGR of 5.92% Due
focus was given in Twelfth Plan on increasing the share of containerized cargo in ports with
a view to capturing a higher share of international trade. A number of projects for rail/road
connectivity were taken up and monitored closely both for Major and non-Major Ports.
(v) Private Sector Participation: In the 12th Plan, the need for working out PPP model for
infrastructure Port development Project was stressed. Active steps have been taken to fully
utilize the potential, resources and professionalism of the private sector. These include
standardization of bidding documents, transparent bidding process for selection of PPP operators
etc. Further 100% FDI is permitted under automatic route in the port sector. These steps have

SHIPPING CORPORATION OF INDIA
Recommendation/Observation
23. The Committee notes the financial performance of SCI. The Committee further notes that the SCI
has now recovered from its losses and has been continuously making profit for the last three years.
However, the Committee fails to understand the reasons for incurring PBT and P AT in negative during
2017-18 (till September 2017). (Para 103)
Reply of the Government
23.1. SCI recovered from its losses due to sustained financial efforts which were, however, not supported
by any revival in the shipping markets. The period of recession in the shipping markets, intertwined with
depressed world economic activity, has lasted over nine years. However, SCI has been performing
reasonably well despite the downturn in the industry. The dynamics of the shipping industry is cyclical
in nature and is subject to vagaries of the market, combined with volatility of the rates. It may be
pertinent to highlight here that the current trough (depression) which the shipping industry has been
facing since 2008 has not yet evened out.
23.2.In 2017-18, PBT/PAT is negative till September 2017 due to steep fall in freight and charter hire
rates under the tanker segment, which is a major contributor to revenue and profit of SCI. The freight
rates are depressed due to overcapacity in the market, resulting into a severe recession in the tanker
market. The charter hire rates of Dry Bulk segment have also not fully revived. Thus, the Company has
been affected by the freight markets, added to which the T&OS division incurred a minor loss due to
loss of operating days on account of off hiring of vessels by ONGC. The benefit of the lower operating
cost in the previous years due to abysmally low crude prices has been wiped out with the steep rise in
bunker cost, which comprises almost 60% of Direct Operating expense for operating the vessels.
23.3.It may be noted that PBT is positive for nine months ending 31st December 2017 and the PAT for
nine months ending 31st December 2017 is marginally negative due to increase in tax liability.
Further Recommendation/Observation
23.4. The Committee notes the reply.

IWT
Recommendation/Observation
33. The Committee notes that the discharge of ballast water also causes pollution. The Committee
recommends that Ministry of Shipping may take up the matter under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan
seriously and strict protocol and control measures may be put in place to prevent pollution. The Ministry
should monitor that the protocol in this regard is strictly adhered to. (Para 154)
Reply of the Government (IWT)
33.1. The Inland Vessels (Prevention and Control of Pollution of Inland Water) Rules, 2016 have been
notified in July, 2016. These rules provide for prohibition to discharge of oil, oily mixture, providing
reception facilities at Inland Port cargo or passenger terminals and prescribes for fitment of oil mixture
treatment equipment on shore and on board vessels in certain cases. These rules are to be implemented
by the State Governments.

19
Reply of the Government
33.2. The Ministry of Shipping is mindful of the fact that the ballast water, carried in ships for maintaining
buoyancy, causes pollution in the sea/ocean. The International Maritime Organisation (IMO), in 2004,
adopted the Ballast Water Management (BWM) Convention with a view to prevent ballast water pollution.
The convention establishes standards and procedures for the management and control of ships' ballast
water and sediments. All ships will also have to carry a ballast water record book and an international
ballast water management certificate. This Convention entered into force internationally on 8 September
2017.
The Ministry of Shipping has already initiated the legislative proposal incorporating the provisions of the
BWM Convention into the Indian statute. These provisions put in place the protocol/standard and control
measures to prevent such pollution and strict monitoring thereof. The provisions include penalty for
violation of statutory provisions, setting up of reception facilities in ports, shipyards etc for ballast water
management. India intends to accede to the BWM convention. The proposal of India's accession to BWM
Convention along with the Merchant Shipping Bill 2016 was approved by the Union Cabinet in its meeting
held on 23rd November 2016.
33.3. The Merchant Shipping Bill 2016, in which the provisions of BWM Convention are incorporated,
was introduced in the Parliament on 16 December 2016 and was referred to the Parliamentary Standing
Committee. The Parliamentary Standing Committee has already presented its report which is processed
in the Ministry in the form of a draft Note for Cabinet containing proposal for official amendments to
the Bill to give effect to the Recommendation/ Observations of the Standing Committee.
33.4. However, the Ministry is not in a position to deal with ballast water pollution under the Swachh
Bharat Abhiyan (SBA) as SBA aims to clean up the streets, roads and infrastructure of India's cities,
smaller towns, and rural areas.
Further Recommendation/Observation
33.5. The Committee notes the reply.

MERCHANT SHIPPING BILL, 2016
Recommendation/Observation
39. The Committee desires that while finalizing the Bill, the Ministry should ensure that the interests
and welfare of the Indian seafarers are safeguarded. (Para 180)
Reply of the Government
39.1. Currently, the legislation which benefit seafarers flowing from International Convention are incorporated
in the Act and these provisions are retained in the Bill. In addition to these benefits, in the Bill, it is
proposed to introduce more reforms for welfare of seafarers which are as follows: Clause 5 of the Bill
provides for Constitution of Seafarer Welfare Board.
(a) In Part V of the Bill the provisions relating to the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006
of the International Labour Organization (ILO) covers aspects like seafarers employment,
minimum age, requirement for medical fitness, employment agreements between seafarers and
employers, regulation of working hours, providing proper accommodation to seafarers, payment
of wages, responsibility towards repatriation of seafarer in case of untoward incident of
stranding/death/disability/injury/sickness of seafarer, death and disability compensation,
establishment of social security measures for seafarers etc. India has ratified the said convention
and incorporated the provisions of the convention in the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958. The
above provisions of Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 are retained in Part V of the Bill.

26
Clause 68 of the Bill empowers central government to draft rules for the employment and
welfare of seafarers in accordance with the Maritime Labour Convention.
(b) In clause 53 of the Bill the training institutes imparting maritime training to seafarers shall be
monitored w.r.t content of the course and method of training, keeping in view the standards
set in STCW convention of 1978 as amended.
(c) Recruitment of Indian Seafarers on foreign flag ships shall be mandatorily done through
authorized agencies to prevent the exploitation of seafarers by unscrupulous elements and
ensure their well being and repatriation in distress situations (sub-clause (2) of Clause 66).
(d) Seafarers held in captivity (including piracy situations) shall continue to receive wages during
the period of captivity, even after expiry of the contract (sub-clause (4) of Clause 69).
(e) Bill provides for Insurance for seafarers engaged on fishing & sailing vessels as well as small
vessels with net tonnage of less than 15 tons.
(f) With the concept of Indian controlled tonnage/BBCD/Substantial ownership, training cum
employment opportunity for seafarer is expected to rise.
39.2. The above amendments are expected to attract the seafarers towards the maritime field by ensuring
quality education and providing a safe working environment as per international standards. It would be
difficult to estimate the expected rise in number of seafarers though.
Further Recommendation/Observation
39.3. The Committee notes the reply.

the situation of 2017-18 is not repeated. As IMU was unable to send any realistic plan or road
map for utilization of funds of ` 154.19 crore for 2018-19 till the finalisation of Budget of
Ministry of Shipping, ` 30.00 crore was proposed as BE 2018-19 keeping in view its ongoing
projects and also to avoid surrender of excess funds at a later stage.
(x) In view of above, it may seen that Ministry intervened at the highest level to take supportive
action and hand holding was done to ensure growth and development of IMU. However, these
initiatives could not be fully taken advantage of by IMU.
Further Recommendation/Observation
6.2. The Committee feels that IMU should be provided adequate financial expertise by the
Ministry of Shipping so that IMU may plan its financial activities in a professional way.

CRUISE SHIPPING
Recommendation/Observation
7. The Committee notes that cruise shipping has potential to earn huge amount of foreign exchange
and generation of employment. The Committee recommends that good passenger amenities should be
provided at the cruise terminals so that the tourists are attracted to visit them. Facilities such as e-visa
should be made available at the cruise terminals for seamless passenger travel. The Committee appreciates
the initiative to reduce tariff and made it uniform across Major Ports. The Committee also recommends
that other major ports such as Cochin, Mumbai etc. may also be encouraged to create more infrastructure
for cruise shipping (Para 172)
Reply of the Government
7.1. At present cruise ship visits 5 major ports in India namely Mumbai Port Trust, Murmogao Port
Trust, New Mangalore Port Trust, Cochin Port Trust and Chennai Port Trust. Apart from extending the
incentives to cruise vessel and providing a hassle free handling of cruise passenger, they are also provided
good passenger amenities at the above ports which includes waiting hall, parking space for car/tour bus
coach parking, security, baggage handling, sorting, identification procedure etc. Apart from that, cruise
passengers are provided facilities like Cafeteria/snack lounge, duty free shops, business centre, space for
office, area dedicated for tourist's information, hotel and travel reservation etc. Standardised operating
Procedures (SOPs) for cruise vessel have been revised and operationalised at the above ports. The e-
visa facilities have been provided at the above five ports where cruise vessels visit. Further cruise
passengers arriving with e-visa are exempted from the requirement of bio-metric enrolment for a period
of three years till 31.12.2020.
7.2. Mumbai Port is upgrading the existing cruise terminal at an estimated cost of ` 300 crores which
is likely to be completed within two years and it will transform the Mumbai into an international cruise
destination. An international cruise terminal is already functional at Cochin. To cater to the bigger cruise
ships, Cochin Port is developing a cruise terminal including a cruise terminal building of 2253SQ M at
Ernakulum wharf at an estimated cost of `25.72 crores with financial assistance of `21.41 crores
sanctioned by the Ministry of Tourism in March, 2017.
Further Recommendation/Observation
7.3. The Committee desires that the Ministry of Shipping should ensure that adequate facilities
are available at the Ports to attract more cruise passengers.

The Report of the Department-Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism
and Culture deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Tourism on the Recommendations/Observations
as contained in its Two Hundred Sixty First Report on Demands for Grants (2018-19) of the Ministry
of Tourism which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 6th March, 2018.
2. The Action Taken Replies were received from the Government on 21st August, 2018, in respect
of all the Observations/Recommendations contained in the 261st Report. The replies have been categorized
as follows:—
(i) Chapter I: Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Ministry:
Para Nos.: 32, 37, 40, 41, 62, 71, 86, 94, 104, 108, 109, 111.

view of the replies of the Ministry:-
Para Nos.: 21, 22, 43, 44, 52, 98.

not been accepted by the Committee:
Para Nos.: 7, 9, 30, 31, 42, 48, 56, 63, 64, 67, 68, 73, 75, 77, 81, 84, 88, 97.
TOTAL: 18
(iv) Chapter IV: Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the final replies of the Ministry
are still awaited.
Paragraph Nos.: 61, 100, 102, 110, 112.

have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished at the earliest.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN
ACCEPTED BY THE MINISTRY
ANNUAL PLAN 2018-19
SW ADESH DARSHAN
Recommendation/Observation
1. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should monitor the progress of the
projects regularly so that the projects do not lag behind as the Committee fears that slow paces in progress
of the Swadesh Darshan Projects may result in cost over runs and result in demand for extra allocations
which would further delay the completion of projects. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Ministry should ensure that the projects are completed within the stipulated time. (Para 32)
Reply of the Ministry
1.1 The implementations of projects sanctioned under the scheme are monitored rigorously by the
Ministry of Tourism. The Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC) chaired by Secretary
(Tourism) and MD chaired by the Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Tourism reviews the progress of
its implementation on a periodic basis. The Ministry also holds regional workshops and Video Conference
meetings with the States and UTs to review the progress of the projects. At working level Swadesh
Darshan Division along with Project Management Consultant (PMC) and Domestic offices of Ministry
monitors the project for Cost, Quality and Schedule. States have been instructed to formulate State level
monitoring committees for monitoring of the projects and they also regularly submit the report. The State
Governments have been advised to submit monthly physical and financial progress report of the projects
to the Ministry. The Ministry has also developed an on line monitoring portal to monitor the real time
physical and financial progress of the projects.
Further Recommendation/Observation
1.2 The Committee notes the reply. The Committee desires that it may be apprised of the
details of the online monitoring portal and the way it functions.
PRASHAD
Recommendation/Observation
2. The Committee notes the projects and funds sanctioned to various States. The Committee is very
much concerned about the possibility of delay in completion of the projects. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that projects received from the State Governments should be processed/ sanctioned in time
so as to avoid any delay and non-utilization of funds. The Committee further recommends that the
progress of these projects need to be monitored regularly to ensure that there is no delay and cost overrun
in the projects. (Para 37)

Reply of the Ministry
2.1 Under PRASHAD scheme the project proposal from State Governments/UTs are evaluated by the
Committees "Mission Directorate" (MD) and "Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee" (CSMC),
through presentation and meetings. After that the revised proposal, based on the points of discussion/
suggestion taken in the meeting is approved and fund is released subject to submission of D.P .R,
availability of funds, receipt of pending utilization certificate against the fund released earlier and adherence
to the scheme guidelines. All the project proposals received from State Govt. are processed in the
Ministry of Tourism.
2.2 Monitoring of projects sanctioned under the scheme is monitored vigorously by the Ministry of
Tourism. The CSMC chaired by Secretary (Tourism) and MD chaired by the Addl. Director General of
the Ministry of Tourism reviews periodically the progress of the projects. The Ministry also holds
regional workshops and Video Conference meetings with the States and UTs to review the progress of
the projects. At working level PRASHAD Division along with PMC and Domestic offices of Ministry
monitors the project for Cost, Quality and Schedule. States have been instructed to formulate State level
monitoring committees for monitoring of the projects and they also regularly submit the report. The State
Governments have been advised to submit monthly physical and financial progress report of the projects
to the Ministry.
Further Recommendation/Observation
2.3 The Committee notes the reply. The Committee desires that the Ministry should ensure
effective monitoring and timely completion of the projects. The Ministry should also devise a
mechanism to reward timely completion of projects and penalise delayed projects.
Recommendation/Observation
3. The Committee is not happy with the progress made in the implementation of the PRASHAD projects
in the States. The percentage financial progress of the majority of projects in various States gives a

between the State Tourism Policy and the Centre Tourism Policy is yet to be bridged. The low
rate of project completion/ implementation is evidence of this. This affects the development of
Tourism projects and results in reduced implementation of schemes. The Committee is of the
opinion that the multiple bureaucratic channels may be more of a hinderance than an effective
solution. The Committee, therefore, recommends that concrete solutions must be devised in
order to ensure a higher rate of project completion and implementation. Tourism boosts economic
activity and has resulted in the economic prosperity of many nations which have tourism as their
main source of revenue. A more efficient system and a higher rate of implementation will
contribute to greater profitability of the Tourism sector benefitting both the Centre and the State
Governments.
PRASHAD
Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee notes that out of the 23 projects sanctioned under the PRASHAD Scheme, 10
projects are delayed. Even the projects sanctioned in the year 2015 could achieve only 2 to 25% except
one project in Punjab. Some of the projects could achieve the physical progress of just 2 or 3%. The
Committee observes that much needs to be done for timely implementation of PRASHAD Scheme which
is a flagship programme of the Ministry of Tourism. (Para 42)
Reply of the Ministry
5.1 The implementations of projects sanctioned under the scheme are monitored rigorously by the
Ministry of Tourism to ensure timely completion of the project. The CSMC chaired by Secretary
(Tourism) and MD chaired by the Addl. Director General of the Ministry of Tourism reviews the
progress of the projects implementation on periodic basis. The Ministry also holds regional workshops
and Video Conference meetings with the States and UTs to review the progress of the projects. At
working level PRASHAD Division along with PMC and Domestic offices of Ministry monitors the project
for Cost, Quality and Schedule. States have been instructed to formulate State level monitoring committees
for monitoring of the projects and they also regularly submit the report. The State Governments have
been advised to submit monthly physical and financial progress report of the projects to the Ministry.
5.2 Delay in the implementation of the project is because of the following problems faced by the State
Governments:-
Land availability
Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) clearance
Delay in tendering process.
Further Recommendation/Observation
5.3 The Committee understands that the road-blocks faced by the State Governments with
regards to completion of projects are largely policy related. In this regard, the Committee is of

18
the opinion that the Ministry, at the Centre, must work to constitute a body with the States in
order to devise a solution to the problems faced by the States in the implementation of the
pending projects. The Committee further desires that studies must be instituted with regards to
various policy-related subjects, so that necessary changes and steps can be taken to work through
or around them. In order to ensure its success, the co-operation of the State Governments is
imperative and the Ministry of Tourism must take the lead in resolving policy- related bottlenecks.
The Committee may be informed about the specific steps taken to speed up work under the
PRASHAD scheme.
ASSISTANCE TO CENTRAL AGENCIES
Recommendation/Observation
6. The Committee recommends that these joint development projects should be implemented immediately
and more railway stations should be included for similar development. The Committee feels that Railways
can play a crucial role in promoting tourism in the country because of its wide reach. (Para 48)
Reply of the Ministry
6.1 Under the Scheme Assistance to Central Agencies, various projects with Ministry of Railways for
Tourism Infrastructure development are funded. The details are as under:
1. Joint Development of Tourist amenities at jointly identified Railway Stations: 26 Railway
Stations have been approved for joint development of tourist amenities under 50:50 cost
sharing basis. Total amount of ` 86.02 crore has been sanctioned since June 2018 for 17
Railway stations of which amount of ` 43.67 crore has been released and UC is pending for
an amount of Rs 15.78 crore for 07 stations.
2. Manufacture of Glass Top Coaches:  Manufacture of 3 Glass top coaches with full financial
assistance of `12.00 crore (Final instalment of `6.00 crore released on 29.06.2017) has been
undertaken as per the followings:
• Glass top Coach is running successfully in Vizag-Arakku Valley Vishakhapatnam, Andhra
Pradesh.
• Glass top Coach is running successfully on Scenic Konkan Railway Route Dadar-Madgaon
Mumbai, Maharashtra
• Coach is due to be rolled out on Badgam- Banihal and Baramulla- Srinagar
3. Development of 3 Railway Station under Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd. (KRCL):
Development of tourism infrastructure at Madgaon, Thivim and Karmali Railway stations in
the state of Goa to Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd. has been sanctioned at a cost of `24.00
Crore (fully funded by Ministry of Tourism), out of which `12.00 Crore has been released
as the first instalment.
6.2 As and when railways stations are identified the same will be added to the list.
Further Recommendation/Observation
6.3 The Committee is pleased to note the progress made in this regard. While applauding the
efforts of the Ministry with regard to increasing connectivity by rail, the Committee would like

19
to reiterate the importance of ensuring that the new and existing railway stations are developed
at par with global standards. Facilities and amenities must be ensured with clean and hygienic
cloak rooms, food courts and restrooms. The Committee would like to point out that over the
years a major complaint of tourists in the country, both domestic and international, have been
the lack of sanitation and hygiene in railway stations and the general stench that overwhelms
one upon entering train stations. The Committee feels that to align with the 'Swachh Bharat
Abhiyan' the Ministry of Tourism should work with the Ministry of Railways to achieve the goals.
The Committee further recommends that new railway stations must be developed in a scientific
manner in order to ensure cleanliness and sanitation. Old and pre-existing stations must be
maintained to ensure cleanliness and world-standard facilities.
MARKET RESEARCH
Recommendation/Observation
7. The Committee notes that the activities undertaken under the head —Market Research mainly
concentrate on activities other than market research to promote tourism. The Committee desires that the
Ministry should engage tourism professional to identify the potential bottlenecks and problems of various
tourism places and tourism related policies. Such researches should lead to innovations and improvements
in promotion of tourism. The Committee feels that we should spend more money on development of
infrastructure which should necessarily follow from such studies and surveys. The Committee therefore,
recommends that the Ministry may inform the Committee about the outcome of these market research and
how the Ministry had been benefited in the area of policy making for development of Tourism. The
Committee is of the view that the Government and industry need to work together towards tourism
development across the country. Hiring people from the industry who are professionals/ experts in their
field will greatly help in the proper implementation of the projects undertaken by the Ministry for tourism
development especially to implement the new initiatives undertaken by the Ministry. (Para 56)
Reply of the Ministry
7.1 The major objectives of the Market Research Professional Services Scheme of the Ministry of
Tourism are the following:
(i) Providing Study/survey based inputs for various policies of the Ministry of Tourism.
(ii) Providing CFA to different States/UTs for conducting surveys/studies for getting inputs for
their policies.
(iii) Promotion of research in the field of Tourism through Central Universities/etc.
(iv) Bringing out research and related Publications of the Ministry of Tourism
7.2 The first 2 components are the major components of the Scheme. Under the scheme, need - based
Surveys/studies are conducted through professional agencies, which are engaged as per GFR. The
findings of the surveys/studies are utilised to the extent possible as policy inputs.
7.3 For instance, in 2016 - 17, the Ministry of Tourism conducted a "Study in Overseas Markets of
Russia, Japan, South Korea, Germany, Turkey and South Africa", in which motivational factors of the
visitors were studied and used for designing international publicity campaigns.

20
7.4 A "Study on Functioning of Tourist Police in States/UTs and Documentation of Best Practices" was
also conducted. This report contained a model for Tourist Police in the form of a guideline. This report
has been shared with the Ministry of Home Affairs as well.
7.5 In 2015-16, the Ministry conducted a "Study of Taxes levied on Tourism sector vis-a-vis Export
Sector". Based on the findings of the Study the Ministry of Tourism moved a case for reduced tax slab
for tourism establishments with the Ministry of Finance. This Study was conducted in close coordination
with the industry.
Surveys are also conducted to assess the macro indicators of the tourism industry, for e.g. a Study
on Adventure Tourism Industry Statistics was conducted to assess the size of Adventure Tourism in
India. Tourism Satellite Account of India (TSAI) gives the contribution of tourism in the GDP of an
economy. Apart from these, Ministry of Tourism has approved Central Financial Assistance (CFA) to
Kerala for 3 year Continuous Tourist Survey. This survey gives centre-wise tourist visits.
7.6 In 2017-18, the Ministry of Tourism granted CFA to Madhya Pradesh for undertaking a Customer
Satisfaction Survey of Accommodation Units owned by the Madhya Pradesh State Tourism Development
Corporation (MPSTDC) and Destination Survey. The major objectives of the 2-fold survey were the
following:
(i) Assessment of Quality of services available and level of delivery as perceived by the guests.
(ii) Overall available infrastructure.
(iii) V alue for money in terms of tariffs charged.
(iv) Satisfaction level of tourists w.r.t. their visit at the destination.
(v) Reason/source of information for visiting destination
7.7 The Ministry has also formulated a methodological guideline for Assessment of Infrastructure Gap
Assessment at tourist destinations. The Ministry has shared these guidelines with all the States / UTs with
a request to follow the same.
Further Recommendation/Observation
7.8 The Committee notes that the Ministry could not understand the thrust of the
recommendation. Thrust of the recommendation was that money should be spent for conducting
research on improving tourism and tourism facilities instead of concentrating on market research.
The reply of the Ministry shows that they are concentrating market research though some
initiatives are there to find out the infrastructure gap assessment. The Committee again reiterates
its recommendation that the market research should give more importance to development of
new tourism places and improvement of facilities at the existing tourism destinations.
BUDDHIST CIRCUIT
Recommendation/Observation
8. The Committee appreciates the steps being taken by the Ministry for development of Interstate
Buddhist Circuit in the country. Buddhist Circuits is one of most promising circuits with large potential

21
for development. Buddhist sites are rich in traditions and places of spiritual significance. As a result,
a large number of people from all over the world visit these places, and hence there is a need to develop
these places and provide facilities to visitors. The Committee, however, wonders whether the allocation
for Buddhist Circuits in BE 2018-19 is adequate for development of such massive project. (Para 63)
Reply of the Ministry
8.1 There is no circuit wise allocation of funds under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme. The BE under
the Swadesh Darshan Scheme during 2018-19 is ` 1100 crore. The Ministry has sanctioned five projects
for ` 361.97 crore under the scheme for development of Buddhist Circuit. The expenditure on these
projects and any new project will be met from the BE of 2018-19.
Further Recommendation/Observation
8.2 The Buddhist Circuit is a certain crowd-puller and more proactive steps should be taken to
ensure that this circuit which is revered the world over receives the respect it deserves. The
Committee feels that this is one of the oldest Circuits and its completion is long due. The
Committee, therefore, further recommends that separate allocations must be made towards the
development of this Circuit and it must be given its due importance.
Recommendation/Observation
9. The Committee feels that the full potential of temples and Buddhist sites in the East and North East
and famous temples in the south have not been explored to the fullest. Majority of the tourist spots in
the country are not accessible to the tourists, both domestic and foreign. This is because of high costs
of travelling, poor connectivity and a series of permissions required for various reasons. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Ministry must address the issues of connectivity and better facilities for
the tourists at Buddhist sites. The Committee feels that we have to focus on those areas which possess
touristic/ historic/ religious importance, and are not connected by rail, road and air. The proper connectivity
will further help to increase foreign exchange earnings from foreign tourists which can further help in
development of that area. (Para 64)
Reply of the Ministry
9.1 The Ministry under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme is focusing on development of tourism infrastructure
under thematic tourist circuits with an objective to enhance the visiting experience of the tourists at the
sites. Since development and promotion of tourist sites is primarily the responsibility of respective State
Government/ UTs, the projects under the scheme are identified in consultation with the State Governments.
For better connectivity to the sites under the scheme the Ministry provides funds for development of
last mile connectivity, passenger terminals and Heliports.
9.2 Under RCS-UDAN Scheme, M/o Tourism has already taken up matter of providing connectivity
between the important routes including those of North Eastern Region and Buddhist circuits. Ministry
of Tourism has also suggested connectivity to destinations of Southern states with prominent locations
of rest of India.
9.3 Further, MoT had requested MHA for relaxation in Protected Area Permit (PAP) and Restricted Area
Permit (RAP) in North-Eastern States for five years at a stretch whereas the same has been allowed by

22
MHA for a period of 2 years till 31st December, 2017 for the entire area of Manipur, Mizoram and
Nagaland from the Protected Area regime notified under the foreigners (Protected Area Order 1958).
9.4 After detailed deliberation, Ministry of Home Affairs vide its circular no. 493 dated 14.09.2017 has
excluded the entry of the state Manipur, Nagaland and Mizoram from the protected area regime for a
period of 5 years i.e., till 31st December, 2022, subject to be withdrawn at any time in case of security
concern. As regards the high cost of travel, it is submitted that it is primarily determined by market
forces. It is expected that once, more service providers come to operate in this region, the cost would
go down.
9.5 Ministry of Tourism is continuously taking up the matters to ease the travel of inbound tourists in
a standing Committee headed by Cabinet Secretary. Most of the matters are therefore getting resolved
in time bound manner.
Further Recommendation/Observation
9.6 The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Ministry towards increasing connectivity in
the North-East and promoting tourism. It has come to the notice of the Committee that the
North-eastern States are abundant in Buddhist relics in terms of temples, architecture, monasteries
etc. Places like Sikkim and regions around Darjeeling have established monasteries and centres
of Buddhist studies. The Committee is disappointed to note that States like Sikkim which have
well developed Buddhist Circuits and Buddhist institutions which work to preserve, promote and
teach Buddhism, have done so independently. The Buddhist Circuit in Sikkim can serve as a
perfect example on how to develop the Buddhist Circuit in other parts of the nation. The
Committee desires that the Ministry should work to include North East in the Buddhist Circuit.
This also conforms with the 'Look East, Act East' policy of the Government.
9.7 A major cause of concern is the lack of connectivity in the Northeast. While UDAN schemes
may facilitate the provision of flight connectivity via planes and helicopters, the last mile connectivity
is missing as most villages in the Northeast still lack the basic facilities in terms of pucca roads,
electricity and internet/mobile connectivity. The Committee feels that the development of
infrastructure vis-a-vis tourism is the need of the hour. This will also serve to promote inclusiveness
among the people in the North east and remove the feeling of exclusion in the pan- Indian
narrative. The Committee, therefore, further recommends that the Ministry of Tourism must
work in consonance with the Ministry of DoNER and its nodal agency viz. the Northeast Council
(NEC) in order to increase and promote tourism in the Northeast.
PROMOTION AND PUBLICITY
OVERSEAS PROMOTION AND PUBLICITY INCLUDING MARKET DEVELOPMENT ASSISTANCE
Recommendations/Observations
10. The Committee notes that Overseas Promotion and Publicity including Market Development Assistance
has been allocated 
`454.24 crore in BE 2018-19 against `297.59 crore in RE 2017-18 whereas the actual
expenses under the head in 2016-17 was `194.44 crore. The Committee notes that the size of the
campaign is increased to have India's Presence in global market for longer duration. Tourism campaigns,

23
like Incredible India 2.0 Campaign, are not only economic tools designed to augment tourist revenues,
but they also provide a privileged platform for advancing geopolitical interests through affective and
symbolic means. We need to spend more money on infrastructure and lesser on advertising. It should not
be a case of raising high expectations with our campaigns but the experience not matching up.
(Para 67)
10.1 The Committee, therefore, recommends that allocation made under this head should be utilized
scrupulously for continuing the overseas campaign so that more foreign tourists are attracted and in turn
help foreign exchange earnings. The Committee again recommends that the Government must have a re-
look into the necessity of various tourism promotion offices abroad and the efficacy of various officials
under Overseas Promotion and Publicity. The Committee also may be furnished with country-wise details
of the spending of the Budget Estimate of `454.24 crore which the Ministry of Tourism has proposed
under Overseas Promotion and Publicity. The Committee reminds that the Incredible India 2.0 Campaign
and the publicity and promotion activities should concentrate more on younger generations and the
generations next. (Para 68)
Reply of the Ministry for Para 67 & 68
10.2 In the Budget Estimate 2018-19 an amount of `1330.03 crore has been earmarked for infrastructure
development and only `589.24 crore has been allocated for promotion and publicity.
10.3 As far as utilizing the funds earmarked for overseas promotion, it is stated that the Incredible India
2.0 campaign promotes various tourism products and destinations of the country through Global Media
Campaign in the Television, Print, Online and Social Media. The medium of Television is being used for
the high reach offered by this medium, whereas in the print media publications only those publications
directly targeting potential travellers are being used. There is greater focus on the Digital Media and
enhanced presence on Social Media Platforms, which would effectively target the younger generations
and generation next. The budget for the Global Media Campaign has been significantly enhanced during
2018-19 which would help in reaching out to larger target audience and increase longevity of the
campaign period.
10.4 Also, Ministry of Tourism (MoT) has decided to re-organize its offices on the basis of an in-depth
analysis to identify main source markets contributing to foreign tourist arrivals by consolidating its 14
overseas India Tourism offices into 8 offices. These offices would be located at New York, Frankfurt,
Moscow, London, Dubai, Singapore, Tokyo and Beijing to function as global marketing hubs to cover
various important source markets.
10.5 Ministry of Tourism releases Global Media Campaign in the International Market. These campaigns
are released in Television, Print, Digital and Social media platforms Globally. Since the campaigns are
released Globally, it is not possible to furnish country wise details of spending of the budget.
Further Recommendation/Observation
10.6 The Committee observes that the Ministry has not promoted paid/ promotional video blogs
which are a trend world over. The Committee feels that this is an effective manner to promote
its tourist places to the consumers via an easily accessible platform, i.e. the internet. It is felt
that products under Niche tourism could especially do with this form of promotion. It is a

24
common practice in other countries to promote medical tourism and other similar platforms.
Their experience via video bloggers serves to educate others who might be interested in a similar
procedure. Thus, it serves to increase its popularity as a destination for Medical Tourism. The
Committee therefore recommends that the Ministry should also seek to identify new and interesting
avenues of promotion of tourism in the country. Promotions must not be limited to hoardings
or stalls but should include experience sharing also.
TRAINING AND SKILL DEVELOPMENT
ASSISTANCE TO IHMS/FCI/IITM
Recommendation/Observation
11. The Committee notes the cuts made in the allocation for assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTMs/NIWS.
The budgetary allocations shows that total allocations could not be utilized by the end of the Plan
period. This is disappointing mainly because Ministry of Tourism is underutilizing the fund meant for
skill development at a time when India is faced with huge shortage of trained and skilled people in the
tourism and hospitality industry. While the Committee is happy that the Ministry have taken steps to
ensure the utilization of the aforesaid funds the Committee strongly feels that we must have functional
linkages with need of the industry and academic institutions specially IHMS, IITM, CCI, NIWS, etc.
(Para 73)
Reply of the Ministry
11.1 During 2017-18 Budget allocation to HRD at BE stage was ` 95.00 crore ( ` 87.00 crore plus
` 8.00 crore for North Eastern Region), which was reduced to ` 90.00 crore at RE stage ( ` 82.00 crore
plus ` 8.00 crore for North Eastern Region). However, due to acute need for funds, a proposal was
moved to get more funds at 4th Supplementary Grant stage. Additional allocation to the tune of ` 20.00
crore was provided through re-appropriation bringing the total allocation during the year to `110 crore
out of this an amount of 110.38 crore was utilized. Further, the Ministry through IHMs, IITTM are
closely associated with industry to cater to the demand of skilled manpower.
Further Recommendation/Observation
11.2 The Committee impresses upon the fact that investment in the skill development in the
industries related to tourism is integral to the development of tourism in the country. The
requirements of the tourism sector in terms of hospitality, hospitality management, catering etc.
and its various branches are specialised in nature and therefore it is integral to provide training
for the same. At the same time, in order to be a renowned tourist destination, it is integral that
the industry must be fed with professionals who are of international repute and this can only be
so, when we are able to provide training that meets the global standards. These institutions apart
from being integral to the development of tourism in the country, also serve to act as facilitators
of employment generation via the various skills imparted. Hence, the Committee reiterates the
need to ensure that the funding to these institutions under the Ministry of Tourism should be
looked as capital investment and, therefore, must be adequately funded. Moreover, partnerships
must be promoted with other international nations/ institutions in order to learn from their best
practices.

25
Recommendation/Observation
12. The Committee is happy to note the focused approach and opening of more institutes for the
purpose. The Committee, however, recommends that the new training institutes proposed to be opened in
the coming years should be on the actual requirement of manpower in each stream. The Committee also
recommends that the States which have performed well in promotion of tourism should get priority while
selecting the places for opening such institutes. The Committee also recommends that private sector
participation wherever unavoidable, need to be regulated and controlled suitably if they fail to achieve
the requisite standard. (Para 75)
Reply of the Ministry
12.1 To establish hospitality management institutes financially assisted by Govt. of India, Ministry of
Tourism, a feasibility study on the proposal is done through NCHMCT in which priorities are given to
the States which have performed well in promotion of tourism and getting more and more tourists or
to increase the access to hospitality and tourism education. At the same time, the NCHMCT has also
opened its academic umbrella for more private institutes and the Govt. of India is also keen to bring more
private institutes under NCHMCT towards quality education in the field of hospitality and fill the gap of
required manpower in future days. Presently, under the academic umbrella of NCHMCT, total 72
institutes are running out of which 21 Institutes are under Central Government and another Institute is
under construction. 24 State IHMs created under the central funding are also under the academic
umbrella of NCHMCT and some more institutes are under construction. 14 private institutes are already
under the academic umbrella of NCHMCT and 7 more institutes will be added from 2018-19 academic
year and it is also expected that more private institutes will come under the umbrella of NCHMCT by
next academic year.
Further Recommendation/Observation
12.2 The Committee appreciates that NCHMCT is opening more and more institutes in the field
of hospitality. At the same time the Committee wants to draw attention to the fact that there
are a number of hospitality chains renowned world over for their hotels and its management
staff. These hotels have their own trainee/ internships programs. The Committee is of the
opinion that the Ministry of Tourism must devise a proposal such that the students in our
institutes may benefit from their expertise based on the highest industry standards. Furthermore,
the Committee recommends that the Ministry should use the experiences borne from States that
have performed well in the promotion of tourism towards encouraging and developing the States
that are lagging behind in this aspect.
TOURISM POLICE
Recommendation/Observation
13. The Committee feels that although tourist police has been officially deployed by several states, the
objective is likely to be achieved once it is strengthened further. In many of the tourist destinations, the
tourism police personnel are not visible. The safety of foreign as well as domestic travelers is a serious
concern that needs to be addressed promptly. The states that have not deployed tourist police need to
take this up on priority, and the ones that already have done so need to monitor and improve its
effectiveness. (Para 77)

26
Reply of the Ministry
13.1 In order to ensure Safety and Security of the tourists, both Inbound and domestic, Ministry of
Tourism has taken up the matter of deployment of Tourist Police with all the State Governments/UTs
and fourteen States/UTs viz. Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Delhi, Himachal
Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana and Odisha
have already deployed Tourists Police in one form or the other.
13.2 Ministry of Tourism is also laying stress on training and sensitizing the tourism police about the
needs/specific requirements of tourists. It has also advised all the State Governments/UTs that tourist
police should be deployed at strategic locations relevant from tourist's point of view and they should be
easily visible and distinguishable for the tourists.
Further Recommendation/Observation
13.3 The safety of tourists, both domestic and international are integral to the success of the
country as a tourist destination, as safety is always the priority which serves to motivate or
demotivate tourists from arriving to our shores. However, the Committee is disappointed to note
the poor response from the States in deploying tourist police. The Committee therefore recommends
that the Ministry of Tourism must work in tandem with the Ministry of Home Affairs and the
State Governments in order to ensure that tourist police are instituted and deployed at strategic
locations from tourist's point of view and where deployed the same must be strengthened.
CAPACITY BUILDING FOR SERVICE PROVIDERS
Recommendation/Observation
14. The Committee notes that the allocation of 
`30.00 crore for capacity building for service providers
during BE 2018-19 has been reduced to almost half of the BE of 2017-18 i.e. `65.00 crore. Also, there
is a steep cut in the allocations from BE `65.00 crore to `46.95 crore at RE stage during 2017-18. The
Committee is not convinced with the justification put forth by the Ministry that for 2018-19 thrust has
been given to infrastructural Scheme of Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD and Publicity & Promotion
resulting in less allocation for Scheme capacity Building for Service Providers. The Committee again
expresses its distress because Ministry of Tourism is underutilizing the fund meant for skill development
at a time when there is huge shortage of trained and skilled people in the tourism and hospitality
industry. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should take steps to provide allocation
adequate enough to meet the requirement of trained personnel to serve the increasing tourism potential
of the country. (Para 81)
Reply of the Ministry
14.1 The recommendations of the Committee have been noted. For the year 2018-19, the Ministry of
Tourism has fixed an annual training target of 1,01,900 persons. Funding of the skill development
programme is done in a staggered manner in three instalments and requirement of additional funds, if
any, would be suitably addressed.
Further Recommendation/Observation
14.2 The Committee reiterates its view that education and skill development in hospitality and
tourism industry should be considered for enhanced infrastructural investment.

27
NORTH EAST
Recommendation/Observation
15. The Committee appreciates the initiatives undertaken by the Ministry of Tourism for development
of the North East Region. The Committee notes that the North Eastern States are getting adequate funds
and recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should seek active participation from the States to get more
projects implemented. The North East Region holds better opportunities to attract more number of tourists
both domestic and foreign. State infrastructure development is of utmost necessary for all sorts of
development and State Governments must be encouraged for sustainable tourism in the North Eastern
States. (Para 84)
Reply of the Ministry
15.1 Ministry of Tourism provides Central Financial Assistance for development of tourism infrastructure
to State Governments/Union Territory Administrations including North Eastern States under the Swadesh
Darshan and PRASHAD Schemes subject to receipt of suitable Detailed Project Reports, availability of
funds, liquidation of pending utilization certificates against the funds released earlier and adherence to the
relevant scheme guidelines.
15.2 Ministry of Tourism has sanctioned 14 projects under different themes including Eco Tourism,
Wildlife and Tribal Circuit under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme for `1267.49 Crore covering all the 8
States in the North Eastern Region. The list of projects sanctioned under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme
is at Annexure III. A project for the "Development of Kamakhya Temple and Pilgrimage Destination in
and around Guwahati" has been sanctioned during the year 2015-16 for an amount of `33.98 Crore under
the PRASHAD Scheme.
15.3 The implementation of projects sanctioned under the above schemes is monitored rigorously by the
Ministry of Tourism. The Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC) chaired by Secretary
(Tourism) and Mission Directorate chaired by the Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Tourism reviews
the progress of the projects implementation on periodic basis. The Ministry also holds regional workshops
and Video Conference meetings with the States and UTs to review the progress of the projects. At
working level Programme Divisions along with PMC and Domestic India tourism Offices monitors the
project for Cost, Quality and Schedule. States have been instructed to formulate State Level Monitoring
Committees for monitoring of the projects and they also regularly submit the report. The State Governments
have been advised to submit monthly physical and financial progress report of the projects to the
Ministry. The Ministry has also developed a portal to online monitor the implementation of the project
sanctioned under Swadesh Darshan Scheme.
15.4 The projects sanctioned in the North Eastern Region under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme are
progressing well. The two projects sanctioned to Arunachal Pradesh, one to Manipur and one to Sikkim
are 85% complete.
15.5 The project sanctioned in the North Eastern Region viz. Development of Kamakhya Temple and
Pilgrimage Destination in and around Guwahati under the PRASHAD Scheme is presently under
implementation.

28
Further Recommendation/Observation
15.6 The Committee notes that the Ministry is implementing various projects in North Eastern
region for promotion of Tourism. However , the Committee observes that, most parts of the North
East do not come under the purview of the PRSHAD Scheme. The Committee recommends that
the MoT should look into the development of tourism in the North East region of the country
in terms of categories under Niche Tourism. For e.g. the abundance of nature in its most pristine
ecology should be promoted under Eco Tourism, its varied culture can be promoted under Rural
Tourism etc. The Committee notes that the North East with its pleasant weather, scenic beauty
and its naturally bestowed pristine topography is a goldmine in terms of tourism, just waiting to
be unearthed. The Committee observes that various festivals like the Hornbill Festival in Nagaland,
Sangai Festival in Manipur, Ziro Festival in Arunachal Pradesh have become major tourist
attractions and attract tourists from both within the country and abroad. Tourists are willing to
undergo precarious road journeys and travel miles in order to be enthralled by the region and
its offerings. It is felt that the region's full potential is yet to be harnessed and is not lacking
in interest from the tourist community. The MoT must work to help develop infrastructure in
the region in terms of connectivity and developing its tertiary sector. The Committee further
recommends that the MoT must coordinate with the Ministry of DoNER and NEC in order to
promote and develop the North East as a tourist destination.
RURAL CIRCUIT
Recommendation/Observation
16. The Committee notes that the Government has sanctioned only one Rural Circuit Theme of Swadesh
Darshan Scheme since the inception of the Scheme in the year 2014-15. The Committee feels that the
Rural Tourism needs to be given impetus by identifying more Rural Circuit Theme of Swadesh Darshan
Scheme and by allocating funds for the Rural Tourism projects for States. Villages should be identified
for priority development involving the local bodies in the management. The Committee, therefore,
recommends the Ministry to focus on development of rural tourism infrastructure involving local
communities in order to promote tourism in rural areas and percolate its socio-economic benefit there.
The Committee would like to reiterate that Government has to take concrete action to ensure that the
benefits of tourism growth under —pro-poor approach should reach the weaker sections of society.
(Para 88)
Reply of the Ministry
16.1 The projects under the scheme are identified in consultation with the State Governments based on
proposals received from them. The Swadesh Darshan schemes aims at integrated development of theme
based tourist circuits in the country. The places proposed to be developed under the scheme involves
special tribal zones, rural areas, eco sensitive zones etc. in the interior parts of the country. While
developing the circuits the interventions are planned with the aim of providing employment to the locals,
improving tourism infrastructure in the region which in turn will help in improving the quality of living
of the locals.

29
Further Recommendation/Observation
16.2 The Committee observes that another major reason for the lack of development in terms
of Rural Tourism is poor connectivity. Villages and the interior parts of States are poorly developed
with lack of pucca roads lacking basic infrastructure. The importance of Rural Tourism may be
impressed upon, as it serves to develop the economy in these regions. A number of examples can
be drawn from regions in the North East which have established themselves as tourist destination
and helped in creating an economy by promoting its tribal culture and community life.
16.3 The Committee reiterates its recommendation that the Ministry should focus on development
of rural tourism infrastructure involving local community. In this regard the Committee feels
that the Ministry of Tourism must work in coordination with the State Governments, Ministry
of Road transport & Highways and the Ministry of Home Affairs in order to develop infrastructure
and improve connectivity in the rural areas of the country.
EXCLUSIVE ZONES IN PUBLIC PRIV ATE PARTNERSHIP (PPP) MODE
Recommendation/Observation
17. The Committee appreciates the initiative taken by the Ministry of tourism for formulation of scheme
guidelines for development offive Special Tourism Zones. Tourism not only creates jobs in the tertiary
sector, it also encourages growth in primary and secondary sectors of industry. Hence, Government should
encourage the participation of the private sector in a big way for all round development of the tourism
sector that has the potential to act as the key driver of inclusive growth. The Committee, however,
recommends that private sector participation wherever unavoidable, needs to be regulated and controlled
suitably. The Committee, further, recommends that the five Special Tourism Zones should spread across
various parts of the country. The Committee desires that the Ministry should keep the Committee updated
on the progress of the scheme. (Para 97)
Reply of the Ministry
17.1 The Ministry submitted the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) note for development of Special
Tourism Zone to MoF seeking approval. The MoF vide letter dated 17th May 2018 has advised the
Ministry to conduct a Project Feasibility Report on the establishment of Special Tourism Zones through
a reputed project design consultant with international exposure covering dimensions such as likely
locations, Greenfield vs Brownfield options, reasons for suitability, manpower requirements, comparison
of various options on potential for employment generation, environmental impact, Models (VGF grants,
equity etc.) and quantum of government subsidy, areas of private sector participation, FDI potential etc.
before it can be considered for approval. The Ministry is in the process of appointment of Consultant
for the above study.
Further Recommendation/Observation
17.2 Five special Tourism Zones is an ambitious project of the Government of India. However,
the Committee notes that the Ministry of Finance refused permission on the ground that proper
studies are not conduct to assess various impacts of creation of Special Tourism Zones and the

notes with dismay that the Ministry has formulated the projects in a premature way without any

the Committee. The Committee recommends that the details and current status of the special

TRAINING CAB DRIVERS AND PREVENTING TOUTS
Recommendation/Observation
4. The hospitality and tourism sector is very sensitive to unruly behavior of service providers especially
the employees of hotels and restaurants, cab drivers etc. The behavior of the drivers at many of the
tourist places are unacceptable as they act as agents of various hotels and restaurants and coerce the
tourist to choose unwanted hotels and restaurants. In this process they are fleecing the tourists. This is
happening at all the railway Station and bus terminals of the tourist destinations especially in Jaipur.
In many areas touts and untrained tourist guides also misguide the tourists and cheat them. The Committee

32
recommends that the Government should take every initiative under the capacity building programmes
to train the cab drivers to be tourist friendly and prevent the touts at tourist destinations. The Committee
feels that we must all realize that one unpleasant trip to India can actually become a great disadvantage
for tourism. The Committee specially highlighted the often rude and annoying behavior of cab/ taxi
drivers. The Committee feels that Government and industry need to work together to create hospitality
and tourism development across the country. (Para 110)

Further Recommendation/Observation
